clean_body: These Secretary of State races are a key focus for next year's elections.| | | | | | In each of these 26 states, the results from these Secretary of State elections will determine not just who holds those offices but how future elections are run and the shape of our democracy as a whole. = | | | | These types of elections always fly under the media's radar, Team, but this year 26 Secretary of State races will shape the future of our elections, redistricting in 2030, and the outcome of the 2028 presidential race.Opponents of voting rights already know this, which is why they’re already pouring money into these elections – and we have to fight back now, while it still makes a difference. Check out this map: = The work to increase voter participation and turnout for these races has to start now, not this summer. We have to build the infrastructure to defend pro-voter initiatives in Arizona, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Nevada, at the same time as we work to flip the script in key battleground states like Georgia, Ohio, and Iowa. = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | Opponents of voting rights have been working on these objectives for years. They've targeted state legislatures and key statewide offices to control the rules around voting and that's why they've been in a position to follow up on the "Big Lie" with bill after bill suppressing the vote. They've played the long game to pick and choose their voters and protect their own power. Most people don't know that their Secretary of State is the state official who runs their elections, let alone who the current office-holder in their state is. But they are the last line of defense against voter suppression and diminished ballot access , which is why we need to invest in voter information, registration, and participation in these critical races. 2025 was a tough year, but we did not back down. Our right to vote is too important and too much is at stake for our democracy, our fellow Americans, and the direction of our country. Driving pro-voting rights voters to the polls in November is the best possible response to all that we've been forced to live through the last decade. = | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. | | Peter,
I wanted to give you the summer off from my emails after you carried me to such a strong victory in early June!
But school is back in session — with my new screen time policy officially in effect — and I got back last week from another very successful session of Camp Harmony (our biggest yet!). And on September 9th, LAUSD’s new camp, which I’ve been working to spearhead, will officially open its doors. It’s hard to believe summer is already over, but there are lots of exciting things to come back to.
I wanted to reach out and invite you to a post-election thank you and service event with **Our Big Kitchen Los Angeles (OBKLA) on Monday, September 14th at 6 PM.**
Sign up here: [https://volunteer.obkla.org/acts/console.php?console_id=0375&console_type=event_list&res_code=pwoBDv&ht=1](https://us.list-manage.com/7FgYvlJl4Z2?e=3cf484ad56&c2id=56d6f92d273ed6c9240a33982acf5cba)
There’s no contribution required; just come join us to make sandwiches, have some refreshments, give back, and spend some time together.
OBKLA is an entirely volunteer-run kitchen that prepares and distributes meals to people in need throughout Los Angeles. I’m excited to partner with them for an evening of service in the Mid-Wilshire area — and to have a chance to thank so many of you who helped make our June victory possible.
Thank you again for your continued support. I hope to see you on the 14th!

| Peter,
Louisiana is the state MAGA has used as a laboratory for its most insidious ideas before shipping them off to the rest of the country.
Earlier this summer, they canceled an ongoing election under a "state of emergency" and eliminated one of our majority-Black Democratic districts.
They passed a bill in the state legislature to force homeless people into indentured servitude. They've criminalized abortions, deployed the National Guard in our streets, and tortured immigrants at the Winn Correctional Center in North Louisiana.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001JNPZlxHcHPVY3dqq0Jkm4aHIvCdHFb54Yznd1bqsbMUiazIzEOgl1Qw_X7ukNYSLs-92HWKhIl9BzE8F1QrqlH8sKpi3IBAPNKk7aYBx24S6IxvlsJwHhcELFBkO0LQlorncbXjlpl6-wlU8-LFBbtjLbOcFaAxS1mDrLxgufSxvKoSUMXZ6KPMqgkBpNP5JtisUErWg8BQAulYGBaEXcXmGU7SLhRFa&c=OLsXZ8KjL8Cc1rPIPSDRMGlLFNknfL-AKu5sdPK5fQsIOPF1JLACPw==&ch=MVM7A7vcazEcm2jHCZ8s73draMPeEHBPQzFot7RTFSAV2lClkhwZPg==)
---
But the four horsemen have arrived in Louisiana and it's a sign of an impending apocalypse...for Donald Trump and MAGA.
The signs are everywhere.
* Trump's approval rating in the state is underwater.

* On May 16th, Democrats turned out in record numbers and delivered a blow that blindsided MAGA, sinking every single one of Governor Landry's amendments by 20 points or more.

* Democrat Jamie Davis just outraised MAGA candidate Julia Letlow in the last fundraising quarter and is now polling within the margin of error against her in the U.S. Senate race.

There's a backlash on the Bayou. Louisianans are tired of being used as lab rats for MAGA's sick and twisted agenda.
MAGA losing their flagship state would be an apocalyptic moment, a tolling of the bell for the most extreme right-wing movement in American history.
Tonight at midnight is our critical end-of-month fundraising deadline and we're $10,267 short of our goal. We're riding on momentum right now in a place where Trump and MAGA least expected, but we need the resources to cross the finish line. That's why we're calling on Democrats everywhere to help us usher in an apocalyptic reckoning for MAGA:
[The Louisiana Democrats are one of the least funded Democratic Parties in the nation and we need your support to carry on this fight. Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Hello! Ready to try Relational Organizing but don't know where to begin? Here's an easy way to jump in! **PAIGE’S FRIEND-TO-FRIEND TEAM** **_Help send a working person to Congress._** Join Paige’s Friend-to-Friend Team and help us reach more voters by talking to five people you already know. Text, call, send a DM, or talk in person. No calling strangers. We do not have millions in corporate PAC money to put Paige on every TV and in every mailbox, so we are doing this person to person. **How it works**
#### 👬 | Choose Five People
Think of five people who trust you and might be open to hearing about Paige. They do not need to support her already.
#### 📲 | Reach Out Your Way
Text, call, send a DM, or talk in person. Use whatever feels natural for that relationship.
#### 💬 | Have a Conversation
Start with why you support Paige, then ask what they care about and listen. You do not need a script or every policy answer.
#### ✅ | Follow Up
We’ll give you the tools to keep track of your conversations and follow up. **Ready to get started?** [Join the Team](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/8NG4xlzuzs4byVaDGNZr25LY9CL8bWmU/click?signature=7d8bc92cafde495b1ab87f4be1d8e31471805b41&url=https%3A%2F%2Fweb2.getempower.com%2Fsignup%2F5-for-paige) Questions? Convicted because of a cooler

| | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. **Now he's fighting for his own freedom** – [**and he needs your help.**](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3qmxSg9LCy86uD0EupOmIZOlKEvVHoFf2PLk94MzmR-Y7eFWUffU75u_YRrS1P_Akep-Xha_bj7My5bnZVtxXLBPUx_XvY-Eg4cSDC8tl8JjyOmdvMIi1gqNMsYUVIvKWhACoCreatcFbZCURtE5pYN10VmpNFnQHVRYpPpYWFopQEAJ-gQGOh0toHBOSGeYKimmPK-n47aVthRpygmHU5jHYqjfcl42Js8MWgbtRmFf6YQTxTkfCQbtQEN8MmgXDFp1MYbIlXo6rsqq4g5t4PgErNBIHUzJZLvn0W_zvgZisnlcXhmYA40U0z4y2Vxu5-_X_zAcglI_Mdl8FIHKf2te_PVybVr_uLz6f2nf_HqcG34_85ef9_vn7DxlmjKTzQH5p4hirePyJw1D2kzFVNmPmD7a5q_-572GvwEAAP__UeCaKw) All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx.

| | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. **Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him.** The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away.[**Will you help Sgt. Duran fight for his freedom?**](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyckcuK3DAQRb9G3qmxSg9LCy86uD0EupOmIZOlKEvVHoFf2PLk94MzmR-Y7eFWUffU75u_YRrS1P_Akep-Xha_bj7My5bnZVtxXLBPUx_XvY-Eg4cSDC8tl8JjyOmdvMIi1gqNMsYUVIvKWhACoCreatcFbZCURtE5pYN10VmpNFnQHVRYpPpYWFopQEAJ-gQGOh0toHBOSGeYKimmPK-n47aVthRpygmHU5jHYqjfcl42Js8MWgbtRmFf6YQTxTkfCQbtQEN8MmgXDFp1MYbIlXo6rsqq4g5t4PgErNBIHUzJZLvn0W_zvgZisnlcXhmYA40U0z4y2Vxu5-_X_zAcglI_Mdl8FIHKf2te_PVybVr_uLz6f2nf_HqcG34_85ef9_vn7DxlmjKTzQH5p4hirePyJw1D2kzFVNmPmD7a5q_-572GvwEAAP__UeCaKw) The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal.But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive.And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. **They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.****Their own lives have been threatened because of this case.** That's why I’m asking for your help today. **[Please make a tax-deductible donation of $35, $50, $100, or more to help fund Sgt. Convicted because of a cooler | | | | | | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal.But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive.And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.Their own lives have been threatened because of this case. name: Greisa, United We Dream
subject: My dad died in exile. I'm still here.
body:
When a family loses someone to detention, a lawyer can change everything. | | | Peter, When I was a teenager, my father, Luis, was racially profiled by local law enforcement in Texas and deported to Mexico. He died in exile in 2024, and I never saw him again. My mother, Elia, passed away because she couldn't access the cancer treatment she needed as an undocumented person. I'm sharing this because I know the desperation of searching for a lawyer for someone you love and not finding one in time. Today, millions of families are living through that same search. As of May, there were **1.7 million pending cases** where people were facing deportation proceedings without a lawyer by their side.1 Even children have stood alone before government prosecutors. **That's why United We Dream went to the ACLU and the Abundant Futures Fund with an idea: build a rapid-response legal defense effort that could quickly scale up access to lawyers.** Together, we launched the **Defending Our Neighbors Fund** , which has raised more than $15 million so far to expand legal representation and enable trusted community legal organizations to take on more clients. **[The Defending Our Neighbors Fund is powered by everyday people like you, stepping up to build a vital lifeline supporting our immigrant neighbors, loved ones, and communities against injustice. **TOP NEWS**
**" Meta to pay Texas $1 billion in child safety case"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/be58a40c-b6a0-4f90-9e82-7d71e9de3889?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Eleanor Klibanoff** - Social media giant Meta will pay over $1 billion to Texas and implement sweeping protections for children as part of a settlement with the state, Attorney General **Ken Paxton** announced Wednesday.

The settlement comes as Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, tentatively agreed to a $17 billion payout to resolve a separate lawsuit brought by 33 states, which Texas was not a part of. The historic settlement, the first of this scale from a social media company, will end the ongoing trial in that case.

The states allege that Meta contributed to the growing youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing their social media platforms to be addicting to kids and teens.

As part of Texas' settlement, Meta will apply stricter age verification measures and institute a daily two-hour limit for teens. All notifications from these platforms will be disabled by default during school hours, and the company will create a nighttime mode to restrict access for teens, Ken Paxton said in a press release. Meta's chief legal officer, **C.J. Mahoney** , said in a statement that the new safety rules will empower parents to manage their children's use of these platforms.

Paxton is also suing TikTok, with that case expected to go to trial in the fall. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/be58a40c-b6a0-4f90-9e82-7d71e9de3889?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas poll shows solid bipartisan opposition to data centers"** via [The Washington Post](https://substack.com/redirect/c0d785d1-5f2f-4c3e-bcc9-d3573b8d40c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Molly Hennessy-Fiske** - A growing backlash against the projects is reshaping important races in the deeply conservative state.

Opposition to data centers has solidified in Texas, with 57 percent of Texas voters saying they do not want them in their community, according to a poll released Tuesday by the University of Texas/Texas Politics Project.

Data centers have roiled the state's politics this cycle as longtime Republicans have broken with their normally pro-business party leaders. Democrats (74 percent) and independents (54 percent) are the most likely to oppose data center construction, the new poll found, but a solid plurality of Republicans (43 percent) have joined their ranks. _([WAPO](https://substack.com/redirect/c0d785d1-5f2f-4c3e-bcc9-d3573b8d40c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Ross Fire has burned in North Texas for three days"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/520ef3a0-401b-4334-a107-21456095aed9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Alejandra Martinez** - The Ross Fire has grown into one of the largest wildfires in the Dallas-Fort Worth area's recorded history, scorching 85,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties in just three days.

The fire, which began Monday near Palo Pinto, grew with extraordinary speed in the dry ranchland. By Tuesday, officials reported that the fire had doubled in size in a few hours to about 50,000 acres. By Wednesday, the estimate had climbed above 80,000 acres.

Firefighters have reported extreme fire behavior, including trees torching in groups amid strong winds. There have been no reports of injuries from the fire, but some rural residents have been advised to evacuate over the past three days and officials told residents in or near affected areas to be prepared to leave quickly if conditions change.

Local officials have closed numerous roads in Palo Pinto County, including parts of U.S. 180 and Texas 254 as crews continue responding to the fire. Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Tuesday that FEMA had approved a Fire Management Assistance Grant for the Ross Fire, which gives local agencies financial help and reimburses eligible firefighting costs. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/520ef3a0-401b-4334-a107-21456095aed9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Capital is Gravitating to Texas"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/a3caa90c-d8ad-4610-a021-fb990bbfa404?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Melissa Brooks** - Texas' rise as a center of business activity is well-documented. Over the past decade, companies across industries have expanded their presence in the state, drawn by its scale, talent base, and operating environment.

**Rachel Racz** , President of Nasdaq Texas, puts it in global terms: "If Texas were its own country, it would be the eighth-largest economy in the world. This isn't a regional story. It's a global one."

The term "Y'all Street," surfaced in discussions about Texas' role in finance, is the descriptor of an emerging ecosystem where issuers, investors, banks, exchanges, and service providers increasingly operate in the same environment.

Goldman Sachs is constructing a new Texas campus designed to house thousands of employees. JPMorgan Chase now employs more people in Texas than in New York. Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Charles Schwab have all deepened their footprint in the Lone Star State. These are not satellite offices. They are strategic anchors. **Ed Knight** , Executive Vice Chairman of Nasdaq, says: "And the uniqueness and the dynamism of the Texas economy is unequaled. **" Flock cameras face growing backlash across Texas counties, but getting rid of them is complicated"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/af593bb4-8550-481b-b785-97efc9a99d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Stephen Simpson** - At a 9 a.m. Harris County Commissioners Court meeting Aug. 17, dozens of Houston residents filed into the courtroom. The commissioners were meeting to review the region's budget, but residents instead came to rally against the county's use of artificial intelligence cameras, many citing privacy issues.

"You promised to protect us, but we see the abuse has come and there's still no protections. We need to eliminate Flock," said **Christopher Rivera** , a member of the Texas Civil Rights Project, to applause from the crowd. Harris County joins numerous counties across the state grappling with community backlash against Flock cameras. Government officials said they understand the community's concerns, but backing out of contracts with AI camera companies is much more complicated than many think since the agreements affect several agencies and jurisdictions.

Atlanta-based Flock Safety is the camera system many counties use and is the company facing the most backlash. Flock uses artificial intelligence to scan every vehicle that passes by a camera, uploading plate numbers, car models, color, and even bumper stickers to the country's largest vehicle surveillance database. Law enforcement agencies that contract with the company -- here and across the U.S. -- can search the accumulated database with a few keystrokes and without a warrant.

The backlash against Flock can't be attributed to any one concern or trend, but rather to a series of recent incidents that have contributed to growing public unease over the extent of law enforcement monitoring. In 2025, a Johnson County sheriff's deputy, without a warrant, used the nationwide network of over 83,000 Flock cameras to track a woman suspected of attempting to get an abortion. The woman was located, but the district attorney's office declined to press charges after a medical examiner found the biological matter in question was a blood clot and not a fetus. The incident sparked national outrage and privacy concerns , and since then the abuse of these systems by law enforcement has been leaking out steadily. Earlier this month, the Harris County Sheriff's Office admitted three of its deputies had been blocked from using Flock cameras while it investigates possible misuse. In Baytown, southeast of Houston, the city's police chief filed a criminal investigation into an officer who was accused of misusing the city's Flock cameras. A sheriff's deputy was suspended in Fort Bend County after looking up one person's plate 41 times and another 148. A Pasadena sergeant resigned after allegedly using Flock to track and stalk a fellow officer, but will not face prosecution. The Deer Park Police Department posted on social media an officer had been suspended after he admitted to misuse. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/af593bb4-8550-481b-b785-97efc9a99d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

Dubbed Starbase, Louisiana, the 125,000-acre complex will dwarf its Texas counterpart with five launch sites that each have two launch towers, fuel and power plants, rocket processing facilities, office buildings, worker housing and its own airport.

"This will be a project like no other, another piece of science fiction transported into reality, or what I call science fact," Shotwell said at Tuesday's announcement. Work is expected to start next year, with the first launch planned for 2029. The project could bring 3,000 to 10,000 jobs to the area known as Pecan Island, about 50 miles south of Lafayette.

Musk said in a post that the Louisiana base "will ultimately have over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day and making it the biggest launch site on Earth!" Louisiana Gov. **Jeff Landry** said "Today, what Elon Musk and his team is offering Louisiana is different. They are offering us a permanent future and lasting prosperity." _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/b798a87e-2efb-4ab1-95a5-a33e2ec15d78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Paramount eyes Austin as potential new base in California exit"** via [Austin American-Statesman](https://substack.com/redirect/4550ed81-07f7-4291-a000-17461842ab7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Ana Gutierrez** - Austin could soon be home to more film and television productions as a major Hollywood studio eyes Texas for a potential move.

Paramount is considering relocating some of its operations out of California as the company fights to close its proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Austin has emerged as a possible destination.

The potential move is far from a done deal. But according to the New York Post , Paramount CEO **David Ellison** and his partners are in discussions about establishing a movie and television studio at the Bluebonnet Business Center at [9219 Old Manor Road](https://substack.com/redirect/24fd460a-4ad0-4fe6-a305-be000578c3d5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in East Austin. _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/4550ed81-07f7-4291-a000-17461842ab7d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Buc-ee's expansion could skip states that don't share its conservative values"** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/2e6c982c-3dcf-403e-9a61-b9efcfc1de5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Rhyma Castillo** - Buc-ee's may be expanding rapidly across the country, but not every state will get a taste of the Texas-born travel center.

Co-founder, President and CEO **Arch Aplin III** discussed the company's expansion plans on Aug. 17 during the grand opening of Buc-ee's 58th store in Benton, Arkansas.

"We have a lot of opportunities. We're growing. We're building in a lot of places, but when you find a conservative, business-friendly state with a phenomenal workforce, it makes a difference," Arch Aplin III said in a video shared by Arkansas Gov. **Sarah Huckabee Sanders**.

The brand has faced criticism over its ties to conservative political causes. According to Transparency USA, Arch Aplin III has donated $882,500 to campaigns supporting Republican candidates and lawmakers. _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/2e6c982c-3dcf-403e-9a61-b9efcfc1de5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Shell puts longtime Houston headquarters on the market for $325M"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/22e913d4-bc3d-44d3-8a99-006274a84483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Marissa Luck** - Shell is planning to sell its nearly 1.5-million-square-foot office campus in Houston's Energy Corridor. Shell's Woodcreek campus has gone through several renovations and expansions over the years. Shell is selling its U.S. headquarters, asking about $325 million for the west Houston campus it has called home for more than four decades.

While the energy giant plans to give up ownership of the buildings, it will maintain a presence on the complex, known as the Woodcreek campus, with a far smaller office footprint. Shell is working with real estate brokerage JLL to market the nearly 1.5 million-square-foot Woodcreek office campus located in the Energy Corridor along Katy Freeway at [150 N Dairy Ashford Road](https://substack.com/redirect/7c3ab148-dcdf-4d0d-aa75-65948f1cda2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

Shell declined to confirm its asking price for the complex, but industry news site Green Street News reported that it is expected to fetch bids starting around $325 million. The Woodcreek campus is being marketed as a sale-leaseback opportunity. Shell would lease a little more than half the campus for 15 years from the new owners, while vacating roughly half the complex, according to marketing materials obtained by the Chronicle. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/22e913d4-bc3d-44d3-8a99-006274a84483?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" IEM picks San Antonio for $200M plant expected to create 3,000 jobs"** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/c204abb0-4fd1-4e5d-a62b-10c834130786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Kelsey Brown** - A California company has picked San Antonio for a $200 million manufacturing plant expected to be the largest job-generating project the city has seen in more than two decades. Industrial Electric Manufacturing is building a 1 million-square-foot factory at Brooks, where the Silicon Valley-based company expects to create 3,000 jobs by 2030.

"IEM is excited to put down roots in San Antonio," CEO **Clayton Such** said. "The city's skilled workforce, strong infrastructure and collaborative economic development environment made this a natural choice for our next phase of growth."

"Bexar County is focused on creating an environment where employers can grow, invest and create opportunity for our residents," **Peter Sakai** said. "IEM's investment reflects the type of advanced manufacturing project that aligns with our long-term economic goals."

**Greg Abbott** said the project highlights the state's role in leading the nation's manufacturing resurgence, noting that a Texas Enterprise Fund grant of $3.36 million is being offered for 448 of the jobs being created.

"This investment by IEM in San Antonio will create new, good-paying jobs and generate a significant economic impact for Bexar County," Abbott said. Brooks Development Authority President and CEO **Leo Gomez** said the South Side investment "didn't just happen overnight." **Sarah Carabias Rush** , president and CEO of Greater:SATX, the regional economic development corporation, said the project reflects "both the scale of opportunity here and the strength of our workforce, advanced manufacturing ecosystem, and collaborative approach to economic development." _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/c204abb0-4fd1-4e5d-a62b-10c834130786?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

TOP NEWS " Meta to pay Texas $1 billion in child safety case" via Eleanor Klibanoff - Social media giant Meta will pay over $1 billion to Texas and implement sweeping protections for children as part of a settlement with the state, Attorney General Ken Paxton announced Wednesday. The settlement comes as Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, tentatively agreed to a $17 billion payout to resolve a separate lawsuit brought by 33 states, which Texas was not a part of. The historic settlement, the first of this scale from a social media company, will end the ongoing trial in that case. The states allege that Meta contributed to the growing youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing their social media platforms to be addicting to kids and teens. As part of Texas' settlement, Meta will apply stricter age verification measures and institute a daily two-hour limit for teens. All notifications from these platforms will be disabled by default during school hours, and the company will create a nighttime mode to restrict access for teens, Ken Paxton said in a press release. Meta's chief legal officer, C.J. Mahoney , said in a statement that the new safety rules will empower parents to manage their children's use of these platforms. Paxton is also suing TikTok, with that case expected to go to trial in the fall. () " Texas poll shows solid bipartisan opposition to data centers" via Molly Hennessy-Fiske - A growing backlash against the projects is reshaping important races in the deeply conservative state. Opposition to data centers has solidified in Texas, with 57 percent of Texas voters saying they do not want them in their community, according to a poll released Tuesday by the University of Texas/Texas Politics Project. Data centers have roiled the state's politics this cycle as longtime Republicans have broken with their normally pro-business party leaders. Democrats (74 percent) and independents (54 percent) are the most likely to oppose data center construction, the new poll found, but a solid plurality of Republicans (43 percent) have joined their ranks. () " Ross Fire has burned in North Texas for three days" via Martinez - The Ross Fire has grown into one of the largest wildfires in the Dallas-Fort Worth area's recorded history, scorching 85,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties in just three days. The fire, which began Monday near Palo Pinto, grew with extraordinary speed in the dry ranchland. By Tuesday, officials reported that the fire had doubled in size in a few hours to about 50,000 acres. By Wednesday, the estimate had climbed above 80,000 acres. Firefighters have reported extreme fire behavior, including trees torching in groups amid strong winds. There have been no reports of injuries from the fire, but some rural residents have been advised to evacuate over the past three days and officials told residents in or near affected areas to be prepared to leave quickly if conditions change. Local officials have closed numerous roads in Palo Pinto County, including parts of U.S. 180 and Texas 254 as crews continue responding to the fire. Gov. Greg Abbott announced Tuesday that FEMA had approved a Fire Management Assistance Grant for the Ross Fire, which gives local agencies financial help and reimburses eligible firefighting costs. () " Capital is Gravitating to Texas" via Melissa Brooks - Texas' rise as a center of business activity is well-documented. Over the past decade, companies across industries have expanded their presence in the state, drawn by its scale, talent base, and operating environment. Rachel Racz , President of Nasdaq Texas, puts it in global terms: "If Texas were its own country, it would be the eighth-largest economy in the world. This isn't a regional story. It's a global one." The term "Y'all Street," surfaced in discussions about Texas' role in finance, is the descriptor of an emerging ecosystem where issuers, investors, banks, exchanges, and service providers increasingly operate in the same environment. Goldman Sachs is constructing a new Texas campus designed to house thousands of employees. JPMorgan Chase now employs more people in Texas than in New York. Wells Fargo, Bank of America, and Charles Schwab have all deepened their footprint in the Lone Star State. These are not satellite offices. They are strategic anchors. Ed Knight , Executive Vice Chairman of Nasdaq, says: "And the uniqueness and the dynamism of the Texas economy is unequaled. The U.S. economy is the dominant economy in the world, and Texas is the dominant part of that economy." () " Texas to receive at least $7.5 billion from stalled border reimbursement fund, Cornyn says" via Gabby Birenbaum -- Texas is set to receive $7.5 billion from a federal fund to reimburse states for border costs incurred when Joe Biden was president, Sen. John Cornyn told The Texas Tribune in an interview, shedding light for the first time on the Lone Star State's haul more than a year after Congress authorized the funding. Cornyn, a Texas Republican who was defeated in his primary this year, said Gov. Greg Abbott and Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin had negotiated the $7.5 billion amount. That accounts for three-quarters of the $10 billion in grant funding that is up for grabs from Mullin's agency. But getting that money into the hands of states has been slow going. The state border reimbursement fund was created in July 2025 in the One, Big Beautiful Bill Act, the tax-and-spending megabill supported by nearly all Republicans and uniformly opposed by Democrats. The bill authorized $13.5 billion in grant funding to state governments, a massive priority for Texas' Republican delegation in Congress and for Cornyn, who pushed for its inclusion during negotiations over the legislation. Texas, which spent over $11 billion on border security through Abbott's Operation Lone Star initiative during the Biden era, has long been expected to receive the lion's share of the funding. Cornyn said Abbott and Mullin worked out the deal "maybe a month ago," but added, "we haven't seen any real movement on that since that time." () " 'Devastating': Texas children's hospitals could lose $2.5B in Medicaid funding" via Nicole Villalpando - Texas children's hospitals are very worried. Changes to Medicaid reimbursements proposed by the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services could significantly alter their funding beginning next year. The Children's Hospital Association of Texas has projected that the state's children's hospitals could lose $2.5 billion a year in funding once the plan by the federal CMS is fully implemented by 2034. The plan, which was introduced this summer, goes beyond the "One Big Beautiful Bill" that Congress passed last year, said association President Christina Hoppe. The Congressional Budget Office originally projected the bill would decrease Medicaid spending nationally by $149 billion from 2026 to 2034, but KFF, the nonprofit health policy organization, predicts CMS' changes would decrease spending $510 billion from 2026 to 2034. CMS has said these changes are necessary to both reduce spending and prevent Medicaid fraud. The CMS plan sets caps on Medicaid funding and reduces state directed payments by between 50% and 80%, the association's analysis found. State directed payments are one way states use federal Medicaid dollars to offset costs that Medicaid service rates do not cover, Christina Hoppe said. "As currently proposed, cuts of this magnitude will restrict access to lifesaving care for children," she said in her letter to CMS last month. Dr. Matias Bruzoni , the chief of pediatric surgery at Texas Children's Hospital North Austin Campus, and Dr. Brian Kaufman , a pediatric orthopedic surgeon, could be impacted by the changes, as could Deb Brown , Dell Children's Medical Center vice president and chief financial officer, who said "It would be devastating," () " Flock cameras face growing backlash across Texas counties, but getting rid of them is complicated" via Stephen Simpson - At a 9 a.m. Harris County Commissioners Court meeting Aug. 17, dozens of Houston residents filed into the courtroom. The commissioners were meeting to review the region's budget, but residents instead came to rally against the county's use of artificial intelligence cameras, many citing privacy issues. "You promised to protect us, but we see the abuse has come and there's still no protections. The firm signed a lease in mid-July to occupy 123,000 square feet in the green, rocket-shaped tower at 1445 Ross Ave. The deal includes an option for Morgan Stanley to increase its footprint as needed. The lease will run for about five years, two people with knowledge of the deal told The Dallas Morning News. The lease is part of a two-pronged development process outlined in city documents. In June, Dallas City Council approved an $18.5 million incentive package and additional tax abatements to support a planned multiphase development that would see the company occupy a new 700,000-square-foot Uptown campus at McKinney Avenue and Fairmount Street. () " Houston postal carriers allegedly helped steal checks worth $23 million" via Wayne Ferguson - Three Houston U.S. Postal Service carriers are accused of helping to steal $23 million worth of checks from the mail they were supposed to deliver. In total, five people were charged as part of the conspiracy, according to an indictment handed up in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas on Aug. 19. According to the indictment, Trystone Tremain Vaughn of Richmond recruited mail carriers to steal checks from mail they were delivering. He then resold the checks to buyers through the messaging app Telegram, according to the indictment. Three mail carriers -- Catherine Clauzell Kilpatrick , Drakkor Jamal Alexander and Malcolm Tiree Joubert -- are alleged to have worked for Trystone Tremain Vaughn from October 2022 to September 2024. () " Hundreds of sweeps later, homeless camps keep coming back. S.A. has a new plan." via Megan Rodriguez - City employees David Row andStephanie Bracely showed up to a recent sweep of a homeless encampment with food, water bottles and a final offer for assistance. Row, the city's homeless outreach manager, and Bracely, an outreach specialist, thought one or two people might still be at the camp. They found the site deserted, most likely because the city warns people who live in a homeless camp that's scheduled to be cleared out days in advance. But it didn't stay deserted. People have returned to the site in the weeks following the clean-up. City officials want to break that cycle with a two-pronged strategy that other cities have experimented with in recent years. First step: stop the sweeps of targeted campsites for up to six weeks and send outreach workers into the camps to help their dwellers find shelter or housing. Second step: clear out the camps and take measures to insure nobody can return to the sites. Mark Carmona , director of the Homeless Services and Strategy Department, said "It has to start with meeting people where they are for a longer period of time," Carmona added, "This decommissioning model is much more intensive on the front end, with more targeted engagement, case management services, identifying the resources, the housing or shelter that's available for them to get people out of the encampment and into a higher level of service," () BUSINESS NEWS " SpaceX unveils $100B Louisiana Starbase that will dwarf South Texas site" via Brandon Lingle - SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell speaks during a Tuesday event announcing a deal to build a new SpaceX spaceport in Louisiana. Elon Musk 's SpaceX revealed plans to build a new $100 billion base for Starship rockets on the southern coast of Louisiana. Dubbed Starbase, Louisiana, the 125,000-acre complex will dwarf its Texas counterpart with five launch sites that each have two launch towers, fuel and power plants, rocket processing facilities, office buildings, worker housing and its own airport. "This will be a project like no other, another piece of science fiction transported into reality, or what I call science fact," Shotwell said at Tuesday's announcement. Work is expected to start next year, with the first launch planned for 2029. The project could bring 3,000 to 10,000 jobs to the area known as Pecan Island, about 50 miles south of Lafayette. Musk said in a post that the Louisiana base "will ultimately have over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day and making it the biggest launch site on Earth!" Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said "Today, what Elon Musk and his team is offering Louisiana is different. They are offering us a permanent future and lasting prosperity." () " Paramount eyes Austin as potential new base in California exit" via Ana Gutierrez - Austin could soon be home to more film and television productions as a major Hollywood studio eyes Texas for a potential move. Paramount is considering relocating some of its operations out of California as the company fights to close its proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Austin has emerged as a possible destination. The potential move is far from a done deal. But according to the New York Post , Paramount CEO David Ellison and his partners are in discussions about establishing a movie and television studio at the Bluebonnet Business Center at in East Austin. () " Buc-ee's expansion could skip states that don't share its conservative values" via Rhyma Castillo - Buc-ee's may be expanding rapidly across the country, but not every state will get a taste of the Texas-born travel center. Co-founder, President and CEO Arch Aplin III discussed the company's expansion plans on Aug. 17 during the grand opening of Buc-ee's 58th store in Benton, Arkansas. "We have a lot of opportunities. We're growing. We're building in a lot of places, but when you find a conservative, business-friendly state with a phenomenal workforce, it makes a difference," Arch Aplin III said in a video shared by Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders. The brand has faced criticism over its ties to conservative political causes. According to Transparency USA, Arch Aplin III has donated $882,500 to campaigns supporting Republican candidates and lawmakers. () " Shell puts longtime Houston headquarters on the market for $325M" via Marissa Luck - Shell is planning to sell its nearly 1.5-million-square-foot office campus in Houston's Energy Corridor. Shell's Woodcreek campus has gone through several renovations and expansions over the years. Shell is selling its U.S. headquarters, asking about $325 million for the west Houston campus it has called home for more than four decades. While the energy giant plans to give up ownership of the buildings, it will maintain a presence on the complex, known as the Woodcreek campus, with a far smaller office footprint. Shell is working with real estate brokerage JLL to market the nearly 1.5 million-square-foot Woodcreek office campus located in the Energy Corridor along Katy Freeway at . Shell declined to confirm its asking price for the complex, but industry news site Green Street News reported that it is expected to fetch bids starting around $325 million. The Woodcreek campus is being marketed as a sale-leaseback opportunity. Shell would lease a little more than half the campus for 15 years from the new owners, while vacating roughly half the complex, according to marketing materials obtained by the Chronicle. () " IEM picks San Antonio for $200M plant expected to create 3,000 jobs" via Kelsey Brown - A California company has picked San Antonio for a $200 million manufacturing plant expected to be the largest job-generating project the city has seen in more than two decades. Industrial Electric Manufacturing is building a 1 million-square-foot factory at Brooks, where the Silicon Valley-based company expects to create 3,000 jobs by 2030. "IEM is excited to put down roots in San Antonio," CEO Clayton Such said. "The city's skilled workforce, strong infrastructure and collaborative economic development environment made this a natural choice for our next phase of growth." "Bexar County is focused on creating an environment where employers can grow, invest and create opportunity for our residents," Peter Sakai said. "IEM's investment reflects the type of advanced manufacturing project that aligns with our long-term economic goals." Greg Abbott said the project highlights the state's role in leading the nation's manufacturing resurgence, noting that a Texas Enterprise Fund grant of $3.36 million is being offered for 448 of the jobs being created. "This investment by IEM in San Antonio will create new, good-paying jobs and generate a significant economic impact for Bexar County," Abbott said. Brooks Development Authority President and CEO Leo Gomez said the South Side investment "didn't just happen overnight." Sarah Carabias Rush , president and CEO of Greater:SATX, the regional economic development corporation, said the project reflects "both the scale of opportunity here and the strength of our workforce, advanced manufacturing ecosystem, and collaborative approach to economic development." **" Meta to pay Texas $1 billion in child safety case"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/ab30aeb9-2f95-42e0-b5f2-b33cc08a7348?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Eleanor Klibanoff** - Social media giant Meta will pay over $1 billion to Texas and implement sweeping protections for children as part of a settlement with the state, Attorney General **Ken Paxton** announced Wednesday.

The settlement comes as Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, tentatively agreed to a $17 billion payout to resolve a separate lawsuit brought by 33 states, which Texas was not a part of. The historic settlement, the first of this scale from a social media company, will end the ongoing trial in that case.

The states allege that Meta contributed to the growing youth mental health crisis by deliberately designing their social media platforms to be addicting to kids and teens.

As part of Texas' settlement, Meta will apply stricter age verification measures and institute a daily two-hour limit for teens. All notifications from these platforms will be disabled by default during school hours, and the company will create a nighttime mode to restrict access for teens, Ken Paxton said in a press release. Meta's chief legal officer, **C.J. Mahoney** , said in a statement that the new safety rules will empower parents to manage their children's use of these platforms.

Paxton is also suing TikTok, with that case expected to go to trial in the fall. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/ab30aeb9-2f95-42e0-b5f2-b33cc08a7348?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Ross Fire has burned in North Texas for three days"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/96ec894c-9f43-4e6d-811e-910e7da21351?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Alejandra Martinez** - The Ross Fire has grown into one of the largest wildfires in the Dallas-Fort Worth area's recorded history, scorching 85,000 acres across Palo Pinto and Jack counties in just three days.

The fire, which began Monday near Palo Pinto, grew with extraordinary speed in the dry ranchland. By Tuesday, officials reported that the fire had doubled in size in a few hours to about 50,000 acres. By Wednesday, the estimate had climbed above 80,000 acres.

Firefighters have reported extreme fire behavior, including trees torching in groups amid strong winds. There have been no reports of injuries from the fire, but some rural residents have been advised to evacuate over the past three days and officials told residents in or near affected areas to be prepared to leave quickly if conditions change.

Local officials have closed numerous roads in Palo Pinto County, including parts of U.S. 180 and Texas 254 as crews continue responding to the fire. Gov. **Greg Abbott** announced Tuesday that FEMA had approved a Fire Management Assistance Grant for the Ross Fire, which gives local agencies financial help and reimburses eligible firefighting costs. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/96ec894c-9f43-4e6d-811e-910e7da21351?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas to receive at least $7.5 billion from stalled border reimbursement fund, Cornyn says"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/f9a27ac9-2fd9-44ad-a657-4b49c0fad9b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Gabby Birenbaum** -- Texas is set to receive $7.5 billion from a federal fund to reimburse states for border costs incurred when **Joe Biden** was president, Sen. **John Cornyn** told The Texas Tribune in an interview, shedding light for the first time on the Lone Star State's haul more than a year after Congress authorized the funding.

Cornyn, a Texas Republican who was defeated in his primary this year, said Gov. **Greg Abbott** and Department of Homeland Security Secretary **Markwayne Mullin** had negotiated the $7.5 billion amount. That accounts for three-quarters of the $10 billion in grant funding that is up for grabs from Mullin's agency.

But getting that money into the hands of states has been slow going. The state border reimbursement fund was created in July 2025 in the One, Big Beautiful Bill Act, the tax-and-spending megabill supported by nearly all Republicans and uniformly opposed by Democrats. The bill authorized $13.5 billion in grant funding to state governments, a massive priority for Texas' Republican delegation in Congress and for Cornyn, who pushed for its inclusion during negotiations over the legislation.

Texas, which spent over $11 billion on border security through Abbott's Operation Lone Star initiative during the Biden era, has long been expected to receive the lion's share of the funding. Cornyn said Abbott and Mullin worked out the deal "maybe a month ago," but added, "we haven't seen any real movement on that since that time." _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/f9a27ac9-2fd9-44ad-a657-4b49c0fad9b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" 'Devastating': Texas children's hospitals could lose $2.5B in Medicaid funding"** via [Austin American-Statesman](https://substack.com/redirect/87f4bd03-a227-4cb6-a7bd-4fcf811556ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Nicole Villalpando** - Texas children's hospitals are very worried. Changes to Medicaid reimbursements proposed by the federal Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services could significantly alter their funding beginning next year.

The Children's Hospital Association of Texas has projected that the state's children's hospitals could lose $2.5 billion a year in funding once the plan by the federal CMS is fully implemented by 2034. The plan, which was introduced this summer, goes beyond the "One Big Beautiful Bill" that Congress passed last year, said association President **Christina Hoppe**. The Congressional Budget Office originally projected the bill would decrease Medicaid spending nationally by $149 billion from 2026 to 2034, but KFF, the nonprofit health policy organization, predicts CMS' changes would decrease spending $510 billion from 2026 to 2034.

CMS has said these changes are necessary to both reduce spending and prevent Medicaid fraud. The CMS plan sets caps on Medicaid funding and reduces state directed payments by between 50% and 80%, the association's analysis found. State directed payments are one way states use federal Medicaid dollars to offset costs that Medicaid service rates do not cover, Christina Hoppe said.

"As currently proposed, cuts of this magnitude will restrict access to lifesaving care for children," she said in her letter to CMS last month. Dr. **Matias Bruzoni** , the chief of pediatric surgery at Texas Children's Hospital North Austin Campus, and Dr. **Brian Kaufman** , a pediatric orthopedic surgeon, could be impacted by the changes, as could **Deb Brown** , Dell Children's Medical Center vice president and chief financial officer, who said "It would be devastating," _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/87f4bd03-a227-4cb6-a7bd-4fcf811556ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Flock cameras face growing backlash across Texas counties, but getting rid of them is complicated"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/1fdf2534-3667-4e29-b499-8c059336f907?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Stephen Simpson** - At a 9 a.m. Harris County Commissioners Court meeting Aug. 17, dozens of Houston residents filed into the courtroom. The commissioners were meeting to review the region's budget, but residents instead came to rally against the county's use of artificial intelligence cameras, many citing privacy issues.

"You promised to protect us, but we see the abuse has come and there's still no protections. We need to eliminate Flock," said **Christopher Rivera** , a member of the Texas Civil Rights Project, to applause from the crowd. Harris County joins numerous counties across the state grappling with community backlash against Flock cameras. Government officials said they understand the community's concerns, but backing out of contracts with AI camera companies is much more complicated than many think since the agreements affect several agencies and jurisdictions.

Atlanta-based Flock Safety is the camera system many counties use and is the company facing the most backlash. Flock uses artificial intelligence to scan every vehicle that passes by a camera, uploading plate numbers, car models, color, and even bumper stickers to the country's largest vehicle surveillance database. Law enforcement agencies that contract with the company -- here and across the U.S. -- can search the accumulated database with a few keystrokes and without a warrant.

The backlash against Flock can't be attributed to any one concern or trend, but rather to a series of recent incidents that have contributed to growing public unease over the extent of law enforcement monitoring. In 2025, a Johnson County sheriff's deputy, without a warrant, used the nationwide network of over 83,000 Flock cameras to track a woman suspected of attempting to get an abortion. The woman was located, but the district attorney's office declined to press charges after a medical examiner found the biological matter in question was a blood clot and not a fetus. The incident sparked national outrage and privacy concerns , and since then the abuse of these systems by law enforcement has been leaking out steadily. Earlier this month, the Harris County Sheriff's Office admitted three of its deputies had been blocked from using Flock cameras while it investigates possible misuse. In Baytown, southeast of Houston, the city's police chief filed a criminal investigation into an officer who was accused of misusing the city's Flock cameras. A sheriff's deputy was suspended in Fort Bend County after looking up one person's plate 41 times and another 148. A Pasadena sergeant resigned after allegedly using Flock to track and stalk a fellow officer, but will not face prosecution. The Deer Park Police Department posted on social media an officer had been suspended after he admitted to misuse. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/1fdf2534-3667-4e29-b499-8c059336f907?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Texas court cuts $43M from Infowars' Alex Jones over Sandy Hook lies"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/0fe432cd-3c22-4d2b-8f34-998bb7075e63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Claire Goodman** - A Texas appeals court on Friday wiped more than $43 million from the damages Infowars founder**Alex Jones** was ordered to pay the parents of a 6-year-old boy killed in the 2012 Sandy Hook school shooting.

The Third Court of Appeals reduced the exemplary, or punitive, damages awarded to **Neil Heslin** and **Scarlett Lewis** from more than $45 million to $1.5 million, according to court documents. The ruling leaves intact about $4.1 million in compensatory damages, bringing the new total to about $5.6 million.

Heslin and Lewis' son, **Jesse** , was among the 20 students and six staff members slain at Sandy Hook Elementary School in Connecticut in December 2012. Gunman **Adam Lanza** was killed by police. Jones later spread conspiracy theories about the massacre through his online Infowars channel.

Heslin sued Jones for defamation and both parents sued for intentional infliction of emotional distress. An Austin jury in 2022 awarded Heslin $110,000 in compensatory damages for defamation and awarded each parent $2 million for emotional distress. Jurors separately awarded more than $45 million in exemplary damages. _([HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/0fe432cd-3c22-4d2b-8f34-998bb7075e63?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" The Texas Activist Putting the Ten Commandments Back Into American Classrooms"** via [WSJ](https://substack.com/redirect/a9cbcb8b-b326-4b17-8a96-9965c3eaf078?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Christopher Kuo** and **Anvee Bhutani** - The vault lies inside a grassy hill, next to the rolling Texas prairie.

In the windowless room, climate controls ensure the humidity remains constant, while a suppression system stands ready to snuff out fires. A bulletproof steel door guards the contents.

One recent August afternoon, a burly security guard pried it open, and **David Barton** , a sprightly 72-year-old conservative political activist, strolled inside to his prized collection: tens of thousands of founding-era American documents and artifacts he values at millions of dollars.

David Barton darted among glass cases and rattled off the highlights of his trove: a Revolutionary War-era shot flask, a 1795 handwritten prayer proclamation from **Samuel Adams** , and what he says is a lock of **George Washington** 's hair. _([WSJ](https://substack.com/redirect/a9cbcb8b-b326-4b17-8a96-9965c3eaf078?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" UT replaces College of Liberal Arts dean with another temporary leader"** via [Austin American-Statesman](https://substack.com/redirect/3fcc3365-fbbc-4007-9548-87135ddd5abc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Lily Kepner** - The University of Texas is replacing College of Liberal Arts interim Dean **David Sosa** in yet another leadership shake-up at the university, according to an email sent Friday afternoon to some faculty in the college.

Sosa was named interim dean in May 2025 and led the college as four ethnic and gender studies departments were closed and folded into the new Department of Social and Cultural Analysis.

**Daniel Brinks** , the college's associate dean for academic and faculty affairs and chair of UT's government department, will be the next temporary leader of the college starting Wednesday through August 2027, according to the email sent by a department chair to faculty.

The change marks more turnover as the College of Liberal Arts enters its second academic year without a permanent leader in place. The last permanent dean was **Ann Stevens** , who said in 2024 that former President **Jay Hartzell** blocked her from a second term leading the college. _([AAS](https://substack.com/redirect/3fcc3365-fbbc-4007-9548-87135ddd5abc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" New Poll: Talarico Holds Lead Against Paxton, While Texas Voters View Democrats Unfavorably"** via [The Texan](https://substack.com/redirect/6dd24366-c61c-49ee-9ec9-0586a1dfb638?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Mary Elise O 'Bar** - A new survey indicates state Rep.**James Talarico** (D-Austin) leads Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** in the U.S. Senate race, even while the majority of Texas voters view the Democratic Party negatively.

Talarico is ahead of Paxton by three percentage points in this new poll, conducted by the Texas Politics Project (TPP) at the University of Texas, although the number of undecided participants alone is enough to sway the race in the other direction.

**" Texas' limits on certain drag shows ruled unconstitutional again"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/556e353f-254e-4645-bf04-d3a9c3e3969d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Ayden Runnels** - Texas once again cannot enforce its restrictions on some public drag shows after a federal judge on Tuesday declared a 2023 law unconstitutional for the second time.

U.S. District Judge **David Hittner** initially declared Senate Bill 12 unconstitutional in September 2023 only a few months after it was passed by the Texas Legislature, citing First Amendment violations. More than two years later in November, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals unblocked the law and returned the case to Hittner with specific instructions on how to reassess it.

Hittner reaffirmed his ruling Tuesday, stating in his order that besides removing several plaintiffs and defendants from the lawsuit, the appellate court's decision "did not disturb" his prior decision declaring SB 12 unconstitutional. The ruling again pauses the law, which had gone into effect in March after the 5th Circuit's decision.

The suit was originally filed against Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** , two counties three district attorneys and one county attorney by two community pride groups, two entertainment groups and **Brigitte Bandit** , a drag queen and longtime Texas LGBTQ+ rights activist. After the 5th Circuit's ruling, the two pride groups were removed as plaintiffs and Paxton was left as the sole defendant, which Hittner said satisfied the higher court's instructions. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/556e353f-254e-4645-bf04-d3a9c3e3969d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

Old Parkland is expanding. The Dallas City Council approved a request from developer Crow Holdings to raise the maximum allowable height at the 21⁄2-acre site bounded by Fairmount Street, Shelby Avenue, Reagan Street and Maple Avenue during its Tuesday meeting. Early plans call for 300,000 square feet of new space and multiple buildings. It's the second phase of Old Parkland East.

**Cody Armbrister** , senior managing director of Crow Holdings Development's office sector, outlined the project during a May meeting with the Oak Lawn Committee. Crow Holdings plans to build a 10-story tower behind two four-story buildings. The 10-story building also includes two companion towers of seven stories, Armbrister said. The project's highest point will be the spire at the top of the tallest tower -- 290 feet. The phase will also include four levels of below-grade parking.

**" Will San Antonio pause new data centers? City Council weighs its options."** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/d8cff9ee-e8ad-43a0-ac33-c609f2c3824c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)' **Kelsey Brown** - The City Council is moving toward tightening its rules on building data centers in San Antonio as pushback against the facilities grows across the state. The council is tackling the issue two weeks after Council Members **Ric Galvan** , **Ivalis Meza Gonzalez** and **Teri Castillo** publicly called for a moratorium -- a freeze on plans and permits for the power-hungry facilities that have been moving into San Antonio.

At this week's specially called meeting, the council decided additional data was needed to determine whether a moratorium was warranted. In the meantime, it's shifting its focus to fine-tuning proposed changes to the city's zoning and land-use codes to better manage the data center boom. "I'm not ready to commit to a moratorium," Mayor **Gina Ortiz Jones** said. "I think there's a lot of things we can do to help ourselves."

The pushback against data centers in San Antonio has been brewing since last year, when Galvan filed a policy proposal asking city staff to explore potential amendments to the city's Unified Development Code that would better regulate the industry and its effects on communities. The comprehensive review was approved in December, and the city has hosted three stakeholder meetings since then, leading to this week's council meeting.

San Antonio is joining a growing list of cities and counties across Texas looking for ways to control the sprawl of data centers that has sparked a public outcry from residents concerned about the facilities' power and water usage and about their effects on the environment and quality of life. On Tuesday, Austin took its first steps toward banning large-scale data centers after earlier approving water-use restrictions for large industrial users. At the state level, Gov. **Greg Abbott** has called on utility regulators to audit data centers looking to connect to the state's electric grid. The audit pauses approvals until it is complete. Last week, the Public Utility Commission approved a timeline pushing completion of the audit to late this year, punting the politically volatile issue until after November midterm elections. _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/d8cff9ee-e8ad-43a0-ac33-c609f2c3824c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Houston postal carriers allegedly helped steal checks worth $23 million"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/a68e00d4-2900-494a-87ca-1272f5aaf1cf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**John Wayne Ferguson** - Three Houston U.S. Postal Service carriers are accused of helping to steal $23 million worth of checks from the mail they were supposed to deliver.

In total, five people were charged as part of the conspiracy, according to an indictment handed up in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Texas on Aug. 19.

According to the indictment, **Trystone Tremain Vaughn** of Richmond recruited mail carriers to steal checks from mail they were delivering. He then resold the checks to buyers through the messaging app Telegram, according to the indictment.

**" Hundreds of sweeps later, homeless camps keep coming back. S.A. has a new plan."** via [San Antonio Express-News](https://substack.com/redirect/b15bfb73-befb-4c51-998d-9ab8830ee629?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Megan Rodriguez** - City employees **David Row** and**Stephanie Bracely** showed up to a recent sweep of a homeless encampment with food, water bottles and a final offer for assistance. Row, the city's homeless outreach manager, and Bracely, an outreach specialist, thought one or two people might still be at the camp.

They found the site deserted, most likely because the city warns people who live in a homeless camp that's scheduled to be cleared out days in advance. But it didn't stay deserted. People have returned to the site in the weeks following the clean-up.

City officials want to break that cycle with a two-pronged strategy that other cities have experimented with in recent years. First step: stop the sweeps of targeted campsites for up to six weeks and send outreach workers into the camps to help their dwellers find shelter or housing. Second step: clear out the camps and take measures to insure nobody can return to the sites.

**Mark Carmona** , director of the Homeless Services and Strategy Department, said "It has to start with meeting people where they are for a longer period of time," Carmona added, "This decommissioning model is much more intensive on the front end, with more targeted engagement, case management services, identifying the resources, the housing or shelter that's available for them to get people out of the encampment and into a higher level of service," _([SAEN](https://substack.com/redirect/b15bfb73-befb-4c51-998d-9ab8830ee629?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_
