Trump’s first appearance for Paxton’s campaign comes in a week when ad spending by Republicans for the state’s attorney general surpassed his Democratic opponents for the first time. The president, who upon deplaning was closely followed by Bill Pulte , the director of U.S. Federal Housing, was greeted by U.S. Rep. Brian Babin , R-Woodville, on the Ellington Field Joint Reserve Base tarmac. The president waved to over a hundred fans who chanted his name and USA before leaving for a Republican National Committee fundraising event, where he is expected to be a keynote speaker rallying support behind the Republican nominee. Trump was expected to headline a Republican National Committee fundraising event Thursday evening during his overnight stay in Houston. On Friday, the president is expected to honor members of the Artemis II lunar flyby crew at the Johnson Space Center. ( ) “Talarico campaign asks court to unseal Paxton’s depositions in energy investing dispute” via ‘sKayla Guo – Democratic U.S. Senate nominee James Talarico’s campaign on Wednesday asked a court to unseal transcripts of a pair of years-old depositions given by his opponent, Attorney GeneralKen Paxton , as part of a messy securities fraud dispute. The petition, filed in Collin County, targets depositions Paxton sat for in 2019 and 2022 as part of a legal clash that ensnared the attorney general, his financial adviser and his former business associates. North Texas businessman Charles Loper III , who oversees Paxton’s blind trust, in 2016 accused an energy company called Unity Resources and two of its investors, Byron Cook and Joel Hochberg , of defrauding him. The case centered in part on alleged securities fraud, with Loper accusing Cook and Hochberg of launching a scheme to profit off a Unity investment fund. Cook and Hochberg in turn accused Loper and Paxton of conspiring to sully their names because they were set to serve as key witnesses in a separate criminal securities fraud case against Paxton. Paxton previously served as a lawyer and board member for Unity and invested in the company. In Paxton’s separate criminal securities fraud case, Cook and Hochberg accused Paxton of misleading them into investing in a McKinney technology company without disclosing he’d be paid a commission for the recruitments. Paxton was indicted in 2015, the year before Loper brought his lawsuit. Prosecutors dropped the charges against Paxton before trial in 2024, under a deal that required him to pay restitution and take legal ethics courses. ( ) “Texas Senate hopeful Talarico teams with Mark Cuban on plan to break up healthcare ‘monopolies’” via ‘sJustin Papp – Texas Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico is out with a new plan to break up what he says are healthcare monopolies and bring down the cost of prescription drugs. And he’s teaming up with entrepreneur Mark Cuban to launch it. Talarico, a member of the Texas House of Representatives who is running against state Attorney General Ken Paxton in one of the most closely-watched Senate races of the 2026 election cycle, will appear with Cuban for a live event and podcast recording in Fort Worth on Saturday to discuss the plan. “Mark and I agree it’s time to break up the Big Medicine monopolies that control our broken healthcare system,” Talarico said in a statement. “Healthcare corporations are ripping us off — jacking up premiums and profiting off our pain. This plan will break up monopolies, lower medical debt, bring down the cost of prescription drugs, and ensure doctors decide what medication their patients need — not insurance companies.” Talarico is trying to become the first Democrat elected statewide in Texas since 1994, in a seat that would be key for the party if they want to win control of the Senate from Republicans. The Cook Political Report with Amy Walter rates the race a “toss-up,” and recent polling shows Talarico and Paxton neck-and-neck. ( ) “Talarico leads young voters, but older Texans may decide the U.S. Senate race” via ‘s John C. Moritz – As he sought to perfect his messaging ahead of entering the race for the U.S. Senate in the summer of 2025, Democrat James Talarico began road-testing a line that still finds its way into nearly every stump speech and cable news appearance more than one year later. “The biggest divide in our politics is not left vs. right,” James Talarico has told audiences from Amarillo to Edinburg, “it’s top vs. bottom.” Largely overlooked inside the charts and crosstabs that explain polling results in the U.S. Senate matchup betweenJames Talarico and Republican nominee Ken Paxton is the yawning gap that divides young and older voters. Put simply, James Talarico decisively leads among voters ages 18 to 49, while Ken Paxton rules among those who are eligible for senior discounts. In the 2018 midterm election, which was the best election cycle Democrats have seen this century, 56% of the votes cast were by Texans 50 and older. The rest were from voters in their 40s and younger, according to stats compiled by Texas political data analyst Derek Ryan. That trend grew even worse for younger voters in the midterms four years later. In 2022, voters 49 and younger accounted for just 41% of total Texas turnout. ( ) “AI’s massive appetite for power, water ignites fight in high-stakes Texas Senate race” via – There’s an ugly political fight brewing in the Lone Star State over data centers, and both candidates running for Senate are racing each other to unveil their plans to slow the AI boom in Texas. Ken Paxton is rolling out his own plan to address what has become a political pressure point in Texas politics during this midterm cycle: how to add guardrails to the explosion of data centers across the state as voters’ concerns rise about skyrocketing power and water costs. “There’s no doubt in my mind that the United States will beat the Chinese Communist Party in the AI race,” Ken Paxton said in a statement. “This plan will ensure that happens while putting Texas First, protecting our culture and land, and safeguarding our families and communities. My plan will also work to ensure that data centers are not utilized to power AI platforms that endanger our children.” James Talarico ‘s political operation, through his Lone Star Rising PAC, has received about $10 million from Reid Hoffman , an advocate for data centers who has argued about the value that they present in the AI arms race against China. “While James Talarico and his campaign infrastructure accept millions of dollars from data center-affiliated donors and put their interests first, I will lead with Texans at the forefront. That’s exactly why I am proud to release my 4-Point Plan that will put Texans First and protect our communities,” Ken Paxton said. ( ) “Paxton promises to ban Chinese technology and chatbots that endanger children in data center platform” via ‘s Samanta Habashy – Attorney General Ken Paxton on Monday pledged to ban Chinese technology from U.S. data centers and hold companies criminally liable if their data centers power AI chatbots that endanger children if elected to the Senate. His data center platform stakes out his position on what has become a flashpoint in Texas’ U.S. Senate race after months of pressure from Democratic opponent James Talarico , who rolled out his plan more than a month ago. Paxton also backed the DATA Act, a bill by Sen. Tom Cotton , R-Arkansas, that would let data centers build off-the-grid power systems exempt from federal regulation, and to champion Gov. Greg Abbott ’s state-level regulatory push — including a repeal of the industry’s sales tax exemptions, among “other outdated incentives,” per the plan. James Talarico , an Austin state representative, has used the GOP’s early support for data center investment as a persistent line of attack, unveiling his “Hold Data Centers Accountable Plan” in July. His plan goes one step further than his GOP opponent, calling for giving local officials approval power over data center projects. ( ) | 2028 “Ted Cruz says on podcast it’s “no secret that I want to be president”” via ‘sGabby Birenbaum – Sen. Ted Cruz , R-Texas, said “it’s no secret that I want to be president” on Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick’s podcast Wednesday as chatter about the 2028 presidential field — and whether Cruz will run — intensifies. Cruz, who finished second in the 2016 Republican presidential primaries to Donald Trump , has served as Texas’ junior senator since 2013. “I will say, this is a bug that history has proved is rarely ended,” Cruz said of his White House aspirations. “It is a permanent and often fatal bug.” Patrick, noting that the GOP 2028 convention will take place in Houston, told Cruz that he “can’t imagine you not being on the stage” given Cruz’s love of politics and debating. ( ) | STATE GOVERNMENT “TxDOT announces $138 billion, 10-year transportation plan” via ‘s Warren Brown – A new 10-year transportation plan with a $138 billion investment behind it was announced Wednesday in a news release issued by the Texas Department of Transportation and Gov. Greg Abbott. Out of the total funding allotted, $95 billion was approved by the Texas Transportation Commission in a meeting on Wednesday as part of the 2027 Unified Transportation Program, or UTP. The remaining $43 billion will go toward development and routine maintenance, the release stated. “This 10-year plan reflects the scale and complexity of meeting Texas’ transportation needs in one of the fastest-growing states in the nation,” said Marc Williams , TxDOT Executive Director in the release. “It is focused on practical outcomes - improving safety, preserving the system we have, and supporting reliable movement for people and goods. The UTP, which is adopted annually, determines how funding for transportation systems across the state is distributed, and give TxDOT and its partners authorization to prepare projects to get under way. Funding will increase for congestion-relief projects that support completed, under-construction and planned non-tolled projects that since 2015 have received $90.6 billion, according to the release. The UTP also includes investments in safety and funding for rural corridors and economic hubs in the Lone Star State. “Texas’ booming economy and growing population demand a transportation system that keeps people and products moving safely and efficiently,” said Gov. Abbott in the release. “This $138 billion investment will strengthen our roadways, reduce congestion, improve safety and support growing communities across Texas. By investing in critical infrastructure today, we are building a bigger, better Texas for generations to come.” ( ) “’Couldn’t find a school’: Why only 76% of Texas’ school voucher recipients have used them” via ‘s Elizabeth Sander and Lawrence Mower – Parents walk with their children to their first day of school at Conroe ISD’s Eissler Elementary School in Conroe, Wednesday, Aug. 13, 2025. Conroe ISD’s use of the state-created Bluebonnet curriculum was part of the reason parentMarissa Gonzalez applied for the Texas Education Freedom Accounts, although she was ultimately unable to use them, joining the 24% of families who received funding and either denied it or haven’t used the award yet. Gonzalez was one of the first parents in Texas to receive funding from the state’s $1 billion private school voucher program. Her two children have dyslexia, and their family income is below 500% of the poverty level, putting them in the lottery’s top priority group. It also meant that her children were eligible to receive more funding than most applicants. But when Gonzalez received $31,000 in voucher funding for her children, she had to turn it down, joining the 24% of recipients who haven’t used their voucher funding — including both families who opted-out and who have not decided yet. The user rate has puzzled leaders of the Texas Education Freedom Account program who are trying to figure out why some families outright rejected or haven’t used thousands of dollars for their children’s education. Still, the rates aren’t far off from what other states have seen, said Joshua Cowen , a professor at Michigan State University who has studied vouchers for 20 years. “The voucher data may seem surprising” he said, adding, “As it turns out, these are pretty predictable phenomena.” So far, 109,000 Texas families have opted in and are using their funding, making the state’s program the second largest in the country in its first year. Still, nearly 25,000 families declined the funding, even after some spent months gathering the materials to apply for it. Another 9,000 families have yet to decide, even though school has already started for most Texans. Abbott said state officials are still investigating whether Christian Castro , who is being held in Cameron County Jail, can be classified as a fugitive because he didn’t flee Minnesota but was apparently reassigned to Texas by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Minnesota is also seeking a court order keeping Castro in custody beyond Thursday for fear he would “flee and avoid prosecution.” In Texas, people awaiting extradition cannot be held longer than 90 days. Castro was arrested in Cameron County on May 29 on a warrant issued by a Minnesota court. Abbott, in a brief filed Monday, asked the judge to deny the request, noting Castro’s freedom would have “no effect on the Governor’s ability to issue a warrant to extradite.” The governor has instructed interim Texas Secretary of State Robert Howden — who was a senior adviser to Abbott before taking on the role — to investigate Castro’s circumstances and whether he should be turned over to Minnesota’s custody. Wynn Rosser , Texas Higher Education Commissioner, said shorter pathways could help students enter high-demand fields a year earlier as well as lower the cost of college. ( ) | #TXLEGE “Texas’ data center, transmission line pauses could be risky” via ‘s Paul Cobler – For the first time in five years since Winter Storm Uri turned the electrical grid into a political albatross for Texas leaders, the state’s grid has again become a liability for politicians. Many residents don’t want data centers in their communities, fearing their massive energy, water and land use, a majority of which is planned for rural Texas. Many residents are also balking at transmission lines lawmakers approved to build hundreds of miles across West Texas because they threaten to eat up their land. The pushback has gotten so overwhelming that the state’s top leaders — the very ones that welcomed these initial proposals with open arms — have called on regulators to delay these projects. “Whatever the complexities of the policies engaged here — and the degree to which the deployment of these high-capacity power lines and the construction of data centers are distinct issues — in this moment, it’s the politics that matter at least as much as the policy,” said Jim Henson , director of the Texas Politics Project at the University of Texas at Austin. ( ) “Texas’ limits on certain drag shows ruled unconstitutional again” via ‘s Ayden Runnels – Texas once again cannot enforce its restrictions on some public drag shows after a federal judge on Tuesday declared a 2023 law unconstitutional for the second time. U.S. District Judge David Hittner initially declared Senate Bill 12 unconstitutional in September 2023 only a few months after it was passed by the Texas Legislature, citing First Amendment violations. More than two years later in November, the 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals unblocked the law and returned the case to Hittner with specific instructions on how to reassess it. Hittner reaffirmed his ruling Tuesday, stating in his order that besides removing several plaintiffs and defendants from the lawsuit, the appellate court’s decision “did not disturb” his prior decision declaring SB 12 unconstitutional. The ruling again pauses the law, which had gone into effect in March after the 5th Circuit’s decision. The suit was originally filed against Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton , two counties three district attorneys and one county attorney by two community pride groups, two entertainment groups and Brigitte Bandit , a drag queen and longtime Texas LGBTQ+ rights activist. After the 5th Circuit’s ruling, the two pride groups were removed as plaintiffs and Paxton was left as the sole defendant, which Hittner said satisfied the higher court’s instructions. ( ) “Former Dem Shawn Thierry appointed to be a Harris County judge” via ‘s Eleanor Klibanoff – Gov. Greg Abbott appointed former state Rep.Shawn Thierry , who left the Democratic party over its stance supporting gender-transition care for minors, to be a Harris County judge on Tuesday. Thierry served four terms in the Texas House as a Democrat representing a Houston district, but lost her primary in 2024 after breaking with her party to back bills that barred doctors from providing transition-related medical care to children and teens. After her defeat, she switched to the Republican Party, where she was warmly embraced. She quickly became the director of political strategy for an international anti-trans policy group, Genspect, and last year, Abbott appointed her to the state’s juvenile justice board. He doubled down on his support for Thierry on Tuesday, naming her to the Harris County judicial bench. She will hear cases in the 515th Judicial District, which was created by the Legislature last session to address the county’s overstretched court dockets. Lawmakers directed Thierry’s court to “give preference to civil cases.” ( ) | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Crickets: Mayor Jones’ plea to outside groups to replace city nonprofit funding falls flat” via ‘sMolly Smith – MayorGina Ortiz Jones didn’t get any takers when she asked area businesses and charitable foundations to step up to fund more than a dozen organizations that have counted on city dollars. Jones had given “business, foundation and philanthropic leaders” she wrote to on July 24 until Aug. 21 to contact her office if they were “interested in funding these worthwhile efforts,” according to a letter she posted on her office’s official Instagram account. Her goal was to close — if only by a relatively small amount — the $158 million budget deficit the city faces over the next two fiscal years by having private-sector dollars replace city grants to local nonprofits and programs. “While there are no financial commitments at this time, I remain focused on exhausting all possible avenues to reduce expenses and explore revenue options, as raising property taxes on our neighbors during this affordability crisis remains my last resort,” Jones said in a statement Monday. ( ) “Old Parkland’s big expansion gets city approval” via ‘s Nick Wooten – One of Dallas’ most exclusive office campuses will get even bigger. Old Parkland is expanding. The Dallas City Council approved a request from developer Crow Holdings to raise the maximum allowable height at the 21⁄2-acre site bounded by Fairmount Street, Shelby Avenue, Reagan Street and Maple Avenue during its Tuesday meeting. Early plans call for 300,000 square feet of new space and multiple buildings. It’s the second phase of Old Parkland East. Cody Armbrister , senior managing director of Crow Holdings Development’s office sector, outlined the project during a May meeting with the Oak Lawn Committee. Crow Holdings plans to build a 10-story tower behind two four-story buildings. The 10-story building also includes two companion towers of seven stories, Armbrister said. The project’s highest point will be the spire at the top of the tallest tower — 290 feet. The phase will also include four levels of below-grade parking. The project’s signature building will be called Tholos, a marble dome that will include statues and artwork celebrating Western civilization. A tholos is a Greco-Roman building type. It is a round structure with a circular wall and roof. One notable example: A tholos sits atop the U.S. Capitol’s cast iron dome. ( ) “Will San Antonio pause new data centers? City Council weighs its options.” via ‘ Kelsey Brown – The City Council is moving toward tightening its rules on building data centers in San Antonio as pushback against the facilities grows across the state. The council is tackling the issue two weeks after Council Members Ric Galvan , Ivalis Meza Gonzalez and Teri Castillo publicly called for a moratorium — a freeze on plans and permits for the power-hungry facilities that have been moving into San Antonio. At this week’s specially called meeting, the council decided additional data was needed to determine whether a moratorium was warranted. In the meantime, it’s shifting its focus to fine-tuning proposed changes to the city’s zoning and land-use codes to better manage the data center boom. “I’m not ready to commit to a moratorium,” Mayor Gina Ortiz Jones said. “I think there’s a lot of things we can do to help ourselves.” The pushback against data centers in San Antonio has been brewing since last year, when Galvan filed a policy proposal asking city staff to explore potential amendments to the city’s Unified Development Code that would better regulate the industry and its effects on communities. The comprehensive review was approved in December, and the city has hosted three stakeholder meetings since then, leading to this week’s council meeting. San Antonio is joining a growing list of cities and counties across Texas looking for ways to control the sprawl of data centers that has sparked a public outcry from residents concerned about the facilities’ power and water usage and about their effects on the environment and quality of life. On Tuesday, Austin took its first steps toward banning large-scale data centers after earlier approving water-use restrictions for large industrial users. At the state level, Gov. Greg Abbott has called on utility regulators to audit data centers looking to connect to the state’s electric grid. The audit pauses approvals until it is complete. Last week, the Public Utility Commission approved a timeline pushing completion of the audit to late this year, punting the politically volatile issue until after November midterm elections. ( ) “Dallas snags Morgan Stanley with huge downtown lease; $1.3B Uptown hub planned” via ‘sNick Wooten – Morgan Stanley has signed a lease for the Fountain Place skyscraper in downtown Dallas — a move that shows North Texas is poised to land the company’s new billion-dollar regional hub. The firm signed a lease in mid-July to occupy 123,000 square feet in the green, rocket-shaped tower at 1445 Ross Ave. The deal includes an option for Morgan Stanley to increase its footprint as needed. The lease will run for about five years, two people with knowledge of the deal told The Dallas Morning News. The lease is part of a two-pronged development process outlined in city documents. In June, Dallas City Council approved an $18.5 million incentive package and additional tax abatements to support a planned multiphase development that would see the company occupy a new 700,000-square-foot Uptown campus at McKinney Avenue and Fairmount Street. ( ) “Hundreds of sweeps later, homeless camps keep coming back. S.A. has a new plan.” via ‘s Megan Rodriguez – City employees David Row andStephanie Bracely showed up to a recent sweep of a homeless encampment with food, water bottles and a final offer for assistance. Row, the city’s homeless outreach manager, and Bracely, an outreach specialist, thought one or two people might still be at the camp. They found the site deserted, most likely because the city warns people who live in a homeless camp that’s scheduled to be cleared out days in advance. But it didn’t stay deserted. People have returned to the site in the weeks following the clean-up. City officials want to break that cycle with a two-pronged strategy that other cities have experimented with in recent years. First step: stop the sweeps of targeted campsites for up to six weeks and send outreach workers into the camps to help their dwellers find shelter or housing. Second step: clear out the camps and take measures to insure nobody can return to the sites. Mark Carmona , director of the Homeless Services and Strategy Department, said “It has to start with meeting people where they are for a longer period of time,” Carmona added, “This decommissioning model is much more intensive on the front end, with more targeted engagement, case management services, identifying the resources, the housing or shelter that’s available for them to get people out of the encampment and into a higher level of service,” ( ) | BUSINESS NEWS “SpaceX unveils $100B Louisiana Starbase that will dwarf South Texas site” via ‘ Brandon Lingle – SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell speaks during a Tuesday event announcing a deal to build a new SpaceX spaceport in Louisiana. Elon Musk ’s SpaceX revealed plans to build a new $100 billion base for Starship rockets on the southern coast of Louisiana. Dubbed Starbase, Louisiana, the 125,000-acre complex will dwarf its Texas counterpart with five launch sites that each have two launch towers, fuel and power plants, rocket processing facilities, office buildings, worker housing and its own airport. “This will be a project like no other, another piece of science fiction transported into reality, or what I call science fact,” Shotwell said at Tuesday’s announcement. Work is expected to start next year, with the first launch planned for 2029. The project could bring 3,000 to 10,000 jobs to the area known as Pecan Island, about 50 miles south of Lafayette. Musk said in a post that the Louisiana base “will ultimately have over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day and making it the biggest launch site on Earth!” Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry said “Today, what Elon Musk and his team is offering Louisiana is different. They are offering us a permanent future and lasting prosperity.” ( ) “Paramount eyes Austin as potential new base in California exit” via ‘s Ana Gutierrez – Austin could soon be home to more film and television productions as a major Hollywood studio eyes Texas for a potential move. Paramount is considering relocating some of its operations out of California as the company fights to close its proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. Austin has emerged as a possible destination. The potential move is far from a done deal. But according to the New York Post , Paramount CEO David Ellison and his partners are in discussions about establishing a movie and television studio at the Bluebonnet Business Center at in East Austin. ( ) “Buc-ee’s expansion could skip states that don’t share its conservative values” via ‘s Rhyma Castillo – Buc-ee’s may be expanding rapidly across the country, but not every state will get a taste of the Texas-born travel center. Co-founder, President and CEO Arch Aplin III discussed the company’s expansion plans on Aug. 17 during the grand opening of Buc-ee’s 58th store in Benton, Arkansas. “We have a lot of opportunities. We’re growing. We’re building in a lot of places, but when you find a conservative, business-friendly state with a phenomenal workforce, it makes a difference,” Arch Aplin III said in a video shared by Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders. The brand has faced criticism over its ties to conservative political causes. According to Transparency USA, Arch Aplin III has donated $882,500 to campaigns supporting Republican candidates and lawmakers. ( ) “Shell puts longtime Houston headquarters on the market for $325M” via ‘s Marissa Luck – Shell is planning to sell its nearly 1.5-million-square-foot office campus in Houston’s Energy Corridor. Shell’s Woodcreek campus has gone through several renovations and expansions over the years. Shell is selling its U.S. headquarters, asking about $325 million for the west Houston campus it has called home for more than four decades. While the energy giant plans to give up ownership of the buildings, it will maintain a presence on the complex, known as the Woodcreek campus, with a far smaller office footprint. Shell is working with real estate brokerage JLL to market the nearly 1.5 million-square-foot Woodcreek office campus located in the Energy Corridor along Katy Freeway at . Shell declined to confirm its asking price for the complex, but industry news site Green Street News reported that it is expected to fetch bids starting around $325 million. The Woodcreek campus is being marketed as a sale-leaseback opportunity. Shell would lease a little more than half the campus for 15 years from the new owners, while vacating roughly half the complex, according to marketing materials obtained by the Chronicle. _**Patriot**_ , I want to tell you about the town I grew up in. Jackson, Georgia isn’t the kind of place that makes national news very often. It’s not a big city. It doesn’t have a famous skyline or a professional sports team. What it has is something a whole lot more valuable, and a whole lot harder to replace. _**It's the kind of town where July 4th is still a big deal.**_ Where folks put flags on their porches not because somebody told them to, **but because they genuinely mean it. ** Where the hardware store owner knows your daddy's name, and where people still hold the door open for strangers without thinking twice about it. Where you can still hear a crowd go quiet when Taps plays at the cemetery. Where the old veterans in the parade get the loudest applause every single time, because every single person standing on that sidewalk understands what those men and women gave up so the rest of us could be there. _That's the America I grew up in._ And I'll tell you, I never took a single day of it for granted. _**Patriot**_ , I think about that America every single day of this campaign. Because here's what I know about Jon Ossoff that I don't think gets said enough: **He doesn't represent that America. ** If he had his way, towns like Jackson would be quietly forgotten, **left behind in favor of the coastal elite's vision of what this country is supposed to look like. ** Diversity committees, government programs, and Washington bureaucrats deciding what's best for people they've never met and communities they've never set foot in. That's not a small disagreement about tax policy, **Patriot**. That is a fundamental difference in what we believe America is supposed to be. This race is about policy, yes. **Ossoff's vote to skyrocket your grocery bill. ** **His vote to send stimulus checks to prisoners and illegal aliens. ** **His votes to let men compete in women's sports. ** **_Those things matter enormously, and I am going to fight him on every single one of them._** But underneath all of that, this race is about something bigger. **It's about what kind of America our kids and grandkids grow up in.** It's about whether the town where a little boy can watch veterans march down Main Street and feel something real in his chest can still exist in twenty years. I believe we can save that America. I believe it's worth every fight, every mile on the road, every dollar raised, and every prayer said between now and November. But I need you with me in this fight, Patriot. **[Will you chip in today and help us fight for the America we both know is worth saving?](http://links.ourdefenseofamerica.com/u/click?_t=aa3ef0db03454a26b650c9ca7e919386&_m=1eda03296df444b994937a3eacc5d7c3&_e=iLgK4KGJexRskIHZMmPQG9RjkdV1oljj2fNKzGPClocSwEdsSfaMGaAGW8pg3I_TzzO34QJ0GHdVXD5xFj_D4OszrNzfDkAHnCMix0zGNBVq-POFwmx4LB-iGYdKKfHjG1KwTqVBLzvWazYBPUv_tw9g695Q6mX8uaYNQsUMQAOM441umzRxEBnX8LdXMsvFxi5jHzCVgJDNNCgTLvm0mMeZPNlWi5gKQEr94fHJKwnHO9xpY7p5ocCpfB_yZao7Gt3Nv6aY8okLRjg52s_THvvmiPy_dT0PCKm6CRjC_qWMt4Dk6FL_kVWEsBEIgto4-haMnDE71Qtb1QkqBChv4KbyYBvq5-QBUQr6t6mb56VUJqzLO_TQ0W4tsksNSMwHpYhNfqBHnX1SsxT5-6gXOddHukei6DyeLK8VeSD8F1khlQy9b4evEh-2FbGJlUz_6Q2wlNLpz4PsWfa2eOhGiLLQ6Wmw9yqBnYj5SfnLzDR6HDZQzbG9rNOYXiuO8kttsYefH-mWOcN3wbugCHWIQv85X7fkyKSTxXpKTUb52Mgi0DcntG5IR7Xi3-tWlfckR9qGU6Tit04516ioOH5mTrtLLJEIUwgyWBXlVDOVRYCX17YfHhBOFQeNBcx_32AD4eHdk5kiV-x-n_mm1eSM3or2eGNCSyScFPLlmIeQzRrvnsJ4dQwAsWsgKwc3Sf3xVXdeSoPMYPgCpxes-F-M2fVovFUzLzuPfMGcXA-R4vk%3D)**

## **THE GOOD: Lionel Messi**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2993403-3615-4dde-acd9-71c6cea5edbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As Lionel Messi announces his retirement from international soccer today, I feel so lucky to have gotten to see this legend play. He won't do it for Argentina anymore, and we'll have to see how much longer, at age 39, he decides to push himself in club play.
I took my then much younger son to see him at The Big House (shout out to David Shuster, Justin Wolfers and Brett Di Resta!) at the University of Michigan almost exactly 7 years ago. Barcelona came for a trip to the U.S. of A. to play against Napoli. We were excited so excited to go...and then Messi got injured, and didn't play.
But...redemption! We got to Messi play vs our FCC Cincinnati warriors after he signed with Miami FC and came to town for the U.S. Open Cup Semifinal on August 23, 2023. Two assists and a PK kick goal that, sadly, secured the win for Miami in overtime. This included a play so classically Messi you felt like you could walk away having seen what you'd come to see--indeed had to see--to say you'd really seen the man play _his game_. In the 68th minute, trailing 2-0, Inter Miami got a free kick on the left side, a good bit outside the penalty box. Messi took the the kick, and didn't put the ball where his teammate was, but exactly in the air in the middle of the box--where he was going to be. A precise, curling cross toward the middle of the penalty box, where striker Leonardo Campana met the ball in the air with his head to put it away. Painful for our team, but greatness.
For a brief moment in a life spent on this spinning beachball in space, we got to see greatness.

## **THE BAD: DONALD TRUMP**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f2993403-3615-4dde-acd9-71c6cea5edbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Folks, as Donald Trump raged against Canada today like an extra in a South Park flick or someone gurgling stupid like he was about to enter a triglyceride-induced coma, I came across a column I wrote about him 15 years ago. 15. God I wish I had been wrong... But the predictions, they were right on. Some nuggets:
> 'Little Donnie Trump, the dumbest kid in the class.' This only somewhat facetious refrain was proffered on a day when Trump had said something particularly insane, by a friend of my parents who attended school with The Donald when they were just boys.
> Trump is a potential presidential candidate who has most recently hitched his hairpiece to Birtherism, or the slightly-less-clever-than-a-comb-over theory that President Obama only plays an American president on TV. In this fantasyland of conspiracy and fear of mind-control via fluorinated water, the president is the amazing beneficiary of the most prescient plot in human history - next to the invention of the hot dog centuries prior to the creation of baseball.
> In Obama's case, it involved the planting of a birth announcement in a Honolulu newspaper to hide his "Kenyaness" and falsely convert him into an American citizen. Because one day, he would inevitably want to be the first black president, and at that moment it sure would come in handy.

But wait, there's more! I went on to tell you _how he 'd do it._ Also, George Santos is back. Join us below the paywall for a Trump prediction I'm stunned I made (I'd forgotten), _and where we won 't have George Santos to kick around anymore..._
More from my take, circa 2011, on our sad sack, spittle-flecked, sponge-bellied shite-pants of a President......

#
Peter, the clock is ticking!
We’re less than **6 hours away** from our August fundraising deadline, and we need all hands on deck to reach our $25,000 goal.
[](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260831-2.5hEpR-&amount=3&refcode=em20260831-536&t=1&akid=536%2E1366028%2EmVKOmB)

name: eric sorensen (personal)
subject: Everyone has their own battle
body:
I’m glad I caught you tonight, Peter. I have a story that might resonate with you:
I’ve been traveling all over the district and recently I had the opportunity to speak with a woman named Betsy. She told me about how she has to travel to the hospital every single month for a procedure.
Since then, I keep thinking about who around me is like “Betsy,” fighting the battle of the day without anyone knowing it.
I’m running for re-election for “Betsy” and everyone like her, but we’re facing our August deadline tonight, and we’re coming up short of our goal. Can you chip in $3 or whatever you can to help us finish the month strong, to keep helping the “Betsy’s” of IL-17?
Here’s a good link: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/es-q3-2026](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138280308/643642239/-1060083271?refcode=em-8.31.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YWI0MWFhYy04ZGE1LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zojJTpL1ojhgYSqxKA5L1nsG_TkXl5-8bMsVIGGx0Yc=)
Think of all of the confidence, perseverance, and strength we may not notice in a stranger's eyes sitting at a stoplight, walking to school, buying groceries, or happily walking into the hospital for the day’s procedure.
**Everyone’s fighting a battle. We need to make sure the people around us are being lifted up instead of being cut down, whether we think they need it or not.**
I didn’t go to Congress just to be a politician or have a title. I went to Congress to represent people like Betsy, my neighbors. And I’ll never let them be treated like pawns for special interests or extremists.
Ahead of our monthly deadline, help me be a good neighbor to them by chipping in $3. Because there is nothing stronger than community power!
Here’s that link again: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/es-q3-2026](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138280309/643642240/-1060083271?refcode=em-8.31.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YWI0MWFhYy04ZGE1LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTlhOGQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=zojJTpL1ojhgYSqxKA5L1nsG_TkXl5-8bMsVIGGx0Yc=)
Thank you in advance for your support.
– Eric

Moline, IL 61265
United States

Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
Thank you for being in it with me.

| I couldn’t let the rest of this day go by without reaching out. And the first thing I wanted to say is _thank you._ Thank you for reading these messages, for spreading the word, and for rejecting the despair this administration is counting on. I know it’s easy to turn away due to the sheer exhaustiveness of this news cycle, but you keep showing up. You keep refusing to give in. That matters. Every time you choose to show up, it gets us one step closer to electing another climate champion — and one step closer to giving communities that have been ignored the accountable leadership they deserve. And we’ve seen it again and again: **when voters have the choice between politicians bankrolled by corporate super PACs vs climate champions accountable to people, more often than not, they’re choosing a climate champion.** We have a whole lot to be proud of, but we need to be _unstoppable_ in these final 63 days until November 3rd. Big Polluters and powerful interests are already lining up behind their bought-and-paid-for candidates. That means _more_ lies, _more_ misinformation, and _more_ attack ads right when our endorsed candidates need to get their message out to voters. clean_body: Convicted because of a coolerConvicted because of a cooler | | | | | | Dear Fellow American,This officer was just convicted of manslaughter for trying to stop a fleeing criminal with non-lethal force. Sgt. Erik Duran dedicated 15 years of his life to the NYPD.He earned dozens of commendations. He helped take illegal guns off the streets. He put his life on the line to protect his community. Now he's fighting for his own freedom – All because of a split-second decision he made during a drug bust in the Bronx. | | | | | An undercover officer had just purchased narcotics from a suspect. As officers moved in to make the arrest, the suspect jumped on a motorized scooter and fled.Duran had only moments to react.He didn't reach for his firearm.He didn't use deadly force. Instead, he grabbed a nearby cooler and threw it into the suspect's path to stop him. The suspect crashed and later died from his injuries.Now, Sgt. Duran has been convicted of manslaughter and sentenced to prison.And he is fighting to clear his name through the appeals process. This appeal is his only chance to avoid spending the next 9 years behind bars with the very criminals he spent his career putting away. The Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund (LELDF) is standing with Sgt. Duran and helping fund his appeal.But legal battles like this are long, difficult, and incredibly expensive.And while Erik fights for his freedom, his wife and children are left carrying the burden alongside him. They’re not only facing the reality of their husband and father spending the next 9 years in prison.Their own lives have been threatened because of this case. That's why I’m asking for your help today. spent 15 years protecting others. Now he needs people like you standing behind him. you for standing with Sgt. Duran. Sincerely, | | | Jason Johnson, President Law Enforcement Legal Defense Fund | | More such officers who sacrifice so much for will face similar fates unless we speak out and stand up for the brave men and women in blue. The next time you see a police officer in your community, please thank them for their service. To read more about our mission or the other Law Enforcement officers we're defending, please visit www.leldf.org. body:
| | | It’s not just the lettuce, Peter. From jalapenos, to blueberries, to eggs and soft cheeses, Americans across the country are wondering how safe their groceries really are after more than 150 food recalls have been issued just this year. This is on top of exploding food prices that have hit working families where it hurts the most: their pocketbooks. The Trump administration’s incompetence, recklessness, and corruption is clearly to blame. **Because whether it’s cyclospora, salmonella, or E. coli, what all of these outbreaks have in common is a food system that is no longer dependable.** Whether you’ve been dealing with these illnesses firsthand, struggling to afford rising grocery prices, or anxiously watching the case numbers go up, we want to hear how this summer’s food safety events have impacted you. **[Can you take the WFP August 2026 Supporter Survey and let us know your thoughts on these outbreaks and their impact on our wallets as we head into the midterms?](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRJ-DmxrOgNSm5J37YZeN7YhYYug3sGysbMy2FRTxm0z-5T2FyhPL9WbT4oBcEuAYCwD7GpZilZC8cdI1RX0bD_k1ZCuSaEs44MQS2EaYcOhItkgygj_j0IetP0h01yDtz-o2gUDQQlPB3SqD7MalFWPf5R-w32L0xcYlf-fK8zfqEhux3rpNWSXvo9I_cFmGaUmyWnNKOtZ-s0CBpMJ7okiAAoON7LqUUvS-gBxdsIKzLk_H63nG6LJsP-w_3lHoe6wJLvRo1ri6AgffXN05MR9a8ORbzlz6q1f67ma_OjsBQ/4tn/Mg2X-LC2RT-Db0dys5BA3g/h0/h001.aBll-ZVca-cGwtwXmMoH1YCSf2UL1vucXKDgwDN6o6A)** **[Take the survey](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRJ-DmxrOgNSm5J37YZeN7YhYYug3sGysbMy2FRTxm0z-5T2FyhPL9WbT4oBcEuAYCwD7GpZilZC8cdI1RX0bD_k1ZCuSaEs44MQS2EaYcOhIl0_V-_KzCbPRVDIYyIk3frSt9-zSN6ClPbim3kaVE2SbjL1kKCzV20xv_isy67IK-l3aZqF7CRleTBqsSBSI5_osuFLu-CcjpH9QviV2SyVoQSnfNruy32focRqh91iBcrw4EVzgv7bTFs5lbpptXoN4qtGRQqsl5SuJNqWwxPHkxUuAVrsAn1f5AwJXTirkQ/4tn/Mg2X-LC2RT-Db0dys5BA3g/h1/h001.fL_v3BJfmqmT1Ybg9VVl-vuSKqh2K2aIMwjRcvV6UhQ)** This scale of crisis is avoidable when our government values expert knowledge and takes action to protect our communities. Unsurprisingly, the Trump administration has done neither of these things. **Since Trump took office again in 2025, he and Secretary of Health and Human Services RFK Jr. have made our system for finding and stopping outbreaks weaker** by cutting budgets and firing experts, as well as delaying a law that could have prevented this outbreak to please his friends at Taylor Farms (who donated $1 million to a MAGA super PAC just 6 days later).1 Our government has the power to make our food both safe and affordable. But while we’ve spent months wondering if we can trust the food that keeps eating up more and more of our paycheck, Trump has continued to spend our taxpayer money cozying up to billionaires, building a ridiculous ballroom, and waging a war in Iran. **We deserve a government that puts our health and safety above vanity projects and corporate profits.** As we fight to elect champions who prioritize keeping our communities healthy and aren’t afraid to stand up to big business: **[Can you take a few minutes to take the WFP August 2026 Supporter Survey and help us understand how members like you have been impacted by the Trump administration’s carelessness towards food safety?](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRJ-DmxrOgNSm5J37YZeN7YhYYug3sGysbMy2FRTxm0z-5T2FyhPL9WbT4oBcEuAYCwD7GpZilZC8cdI1RX0bD_k1ZCuSaEs44MQS2EaYcOhIjCvLch9j2-zkaK7FJVQ_-ciMHuIA9K2yLaIq1W0omS_fk2gaj7DusEfHrBV0wPlbHD3R5jE7VqySBO34PQzhWz2WiO-buwPdkYEjABsg1k_qsaFFV-dJE7TvNWfrKj6judwV3MUngkft8AlbQvAH7r-Rd10jxqKShHsa7rS3hSwn-PjF2igcFAft1XN4qN8eg/4tn/Mg2X-LC2RT-Db0dys5BA3g/h2/h001.zwhsENB285dEk5RYCin-3W6Br5XnWZbif3KNXVvfcsA)** **[Take the survey](https://an.workingfamilies.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoe1DuqQbjt4KoloTZxD-XRJ-DmxrOgNSm5J37YZeN7YhYYug3sGysbMy2FRTxm0z-5T2FyhPL9WbT4oBcEuAYCwD7GpZilZC8cdI1RX0bD_k1ZCuSaEs44MQS2EaYcOhIqzwHLTZ9sp8CaYury8brhgqpOWvaP_WIFqbXeRawPefUaoC80-Pq8sUWBSA9eIe7yl8XZRhdcOoVZB5yPTw9x66xKDzZHidiUz6jJD8I9qm7N5UFbMR6lhhnn0udz6wkb38ObMHH2X07IdmNkMNKRJi04oOdqSRrQWhcg5cq7V8lDYy1eKryI8pxzWjup0iSA/4tn/Mg2X-LC2RT-Db0dys5BA3g/h3/h001.FBWCyRDO3-ePlh_cjdgA9eP41qBr3rRtKsuC46MamJs)** In solidarity, Team WFP Source: 1\. clean_body: | | | It’s not just the lettuce, Peter. From jalapenos, to blueberries, to eggs and soft cheeses, Americans across the country are wondering how safe their groceries really are after more than 150 food recalls have been issued just this year. This is on top of exploding food prices that have hit working families where it hurts the most: their pocketbooks. The Trump administration’s incompetence, recklessness, and corruption is clearly to blame. Because whether it’s cyclospora, salmonella, or E. coli, what all of these outbreaks have in common is a food system that is no longer dependable. Whether you’ve been dealing with these illnesses firsthand, struggling to afford rising grocery prices, or anxiously watching the case numbers go up, we want to hear how this summer’s food safety events have impacted you. This scale of crisis is avoidable when our government values expert knowledge and takes action to protect our communities. Unsurprisingly, the Trump administration has done neither of these things. Since Trump took office again in 2025, he and Secretary of Health and Human Services RFK Jr. have made our system for finding and stopping outbreaks weaker by cutting budgets and firing experts, as well as delaying a law that could have prevented this outbreak to please his friends at Taylor Farms (who donated $1 million to a MAGA super PAC just 6 days later).1 Our government has the power to make our food both safe and affordable. But while we’ve spent months wondering if we can trust the food that keeps eating up more and more of our paycheck, Trump has continued to spend our taxpayer money cozying up to billionaires, building a ridiculous ballroom, and waging a war in Iran. We deserve a government that puts our health and safety above vanity projects and corporate profits. As we fight to elect champions who prioritize keeping our communities healthy and aren’t afraid to stand up to big business: In solidarity, Team WFP Source: 1\. , PBS News, August 16, 2026 Thoughts? | | Friends,

After a decade of hard work, we have achieved an enormous victory!

**I was proud to recently announce that the site of a proposed asphalt plant along the Cedar River has been officially purchased by King County. The land will now be preserved for public use.**

This was a long and difficult fight, but we've stood together since the beginning. And in the midst of all the protests, letters, and moratoriums, I was drafting legislation to purchase and preserve land along this corridor. Now, five years after I first drafted that legislation, we were able to make it happen.
**[READ THE KOMO NEWS STORY HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/Pf_52sfDsmj?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)** [](https://us.list-manage.com/WY6UlKMl0zC?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) **_" This is a fight we as a community have been waging for nearly a decade to protect our river, our natural habitats, and our community. Today, that fight has finally come to an end, and we can shift our focus from stopping what shouldn't be to building what should -- parks, open spaces, and a place the public can enjoy for generations."
\- Councilmember Reagan Dunn_**
**\------------------------
[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/bRIt2c43Qi2?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)
\------------------------**
**This is what fighting for our community looks like.** It took creativity, collaboration, negotiation, and a lot of time and sweat, but, like all of you, I would do it all over again if I had to.

Wins like this demonstrate why we can never give up -- _future generations are relying on us_.

**But I need your help. Would you consider**[**making a contribution of $35, $50, $75 or more**](https://us.list-manage.com/pObSlDGT_cv?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)** to help me continue protecting our neighborhoods, open spaces, and public resources?**
With [your help](https://us.list-manage.com/A8c7Hzt55Wt?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166), I won't stop securing wins for our community!

Thank you for your support! Reagan Dunn

Peter,I just wanted to take a moment to say thank you. Your unwavering support means the world to me.
Because of your dedication, I can keep fighting for our shared values in the Senate. Whether it is advocating for sensible economic policies, defending our national security, or ensuring Maine's interests are always front and center, your backing gives me the strength to do what is right for our state and our country.
We have important work ahead of us. There are critical issues facing our communities, and we must remain focused on delivering real results. Knowing I have you in my corner gives me absolute confidence that we can tackle these challenges head-on.

| | **_Meet Kat_** Kat Cammack is currently serving her third term representing the FREE state of Florida in the People’s House as FL-03’s Congresswoman. She’s running for re-election this year to safeguard our Constitutional rights, preserve our razor-thin Republican House majority, and advance President Trump’s America First agenda in Washington at all costs. Kat’s road from the small cattle ranch she grew up on to the halls of Congress in our nation’s capital has been far from ordinary. A third-generation commercial sandblaster, she originally aspired to take over her family’s business and continue the rural, rodeo lifestyle she had grown so accustomed to. That was until a failed Obama-era housing policy caused Kat’s family to lose their ranch, leaving her and her mother homeless. They lived in their car and bounced from cheap motel to cheap motel just to keep a roof over their heads. But overcoming these hardships moulded Kat into the gritty and unapologetic leader she is today. After her family’s livelihood was destroyed by big government, she made it her life mission to deliver federal reform in the DC Swamp for the American people. And after becoming a mother last year, Kat’s tenacity to fight for America’s freedom has reached new heights. She’s determined to deliver real, meaningful reforms in our nation’s capital that preserve the American Dream for future generations. Kat Cammack has introduced some of the largest tax cuts and regulatory reform initiatives in American history. Simply put, Kat won’t back down until we truly have a government BY the people, FOR the people once again. When she’s not going toe-to-toe with the Washington Swamp, Kat is dedicating every minute to raising, loving, and nurturing her baby daughter alongside her loving husband, Matt. In the little free time they have, you’ll find them tending to their many pets & farm animals, or catching a Florida Gators football game in Gainesville. They are incredibly proud to call North Central Florida’s “Gator Nation” home. Go Gators, and let’s keep Florida America’s bastion of FREEDOM for years to come.

There is a particular kind of theater that plays out in city council chambers across America. It follows a script so predictable it barely changes from state to state, issue to issue. Hundreds of residents cram into folding chairs and overflow hallways. They clutch handwritten note cards, phone cameras ready to livestream. They speak for two minutes each, voices quavering with anger or conviction. They cite traffic studies and constitutional rights. They invoke their children and their property values. They stay until midnight. And then the council votes, often by lopsided margins, to do exactly what the crowd came to stop.
In the past two years, this script has been performed with remarkable regularity around three classes of development that could hardly seem more different: hulking data centers, networked surveillance cameras, and houses of worship. What binds them is not politics or theology, but architecture--the architecture of local government that invites public comment, absorbs it with bureaucratic patience, and then builds over it.

I wanted to send a quick note before the clock hits midnight.

If your inbox looks anything like mine, it’s probably full of “URGENT” end-of-month fundraising appeals.

The truth is, August is a slow month for political fundraising, so many campaigns pull out all the stops to bring in a few extra dollars. Our fundraising is no exception to the summer slowdown, which is why I’m writing to ask you to **_[chip in before midnight](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138282358/643644923/1833629142?refcode=cls-em-fr-20260831-EOM3-365do-l1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjBlYzg0ZWItOGZhNS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NDeKsqyiNqwaeObK1P0MkT7tkpduZkkXrPJjGFASkEI=)_**.

**I’m asking for your support because I know that our community is united in wanting to build a better world – and I’m confident that together, we can elect a Democratic majority and deliver real results for working families**.

**_[But in order to make that happen, we need to raise the money necessary to mobilize voters and win big in November. Will you chip in today to help us build progress up and down California?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138282359/643644924/1833629142?refcode=cls-em-fr-20260831-EOM3-365do-l2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDQ0NDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjBlYzg0ZWItOGZhNS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=NDeKsqyiNqwaeObK1P0MkT7tkpduZkkXrPJjGFASkEI=)_**

A firm belief of mine, one that I’ve repeated often in my travels, is that there is no such thing as a permanently red state. North Carolina is a state that perfectly encapsulates that truth – and tells the story of how on-the-ground organizing, combined with exceptional candidates, can make any community competitive over time.
Roy Cooper is someone deeply rooted in the place that he is running. He has never lost a race in North Carolina – even in years when Trump carried the state. That fact gives me all the more confidence that this November, he can do it again.
[**_That’s not the only reason Roy has my full support for U.S. Senate, but it is why I’m asking you to join me by chipping in to his campaign before his end-of-month deadline tonight. There’s no way to end the GOP’s one-party rule without flipping this battleground seat, but he needs grassroots support to defend himself against attacks and take his message directly to voters._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1347&amount=5&t=9&akid=3116%2E124072%2EimP6sa)

It’s clear to anyone paying attention that the status quo is no longer working for working people. Yet while so many struggle to afford the bare necessities, Republicans in Washington are prioritizing tax breaks for the wealthiest instead of delivering results for the voters who trusted them with power.

name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: New Poll: Is NM’s Governor Race Suddenly Competitive?
body:
Hull closes the gap, NM has billions but could lose population, ICE arrests surge — plus our tribute to Dolly. | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/kg5nMSWAKu4?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
New Poll: Is NM’s Governor Race Suddenly Competitive?
A new poll just turned New Mexico’s governor race into something worth watching VERY closely. Greg Hull is now just six points behind Deb Haaland in the latest Albuquerque Journal poll — despite an enormous fundraising disadvantage and a general election campaign that has been remarkably quiet so far.
And that’s only where today’s show starts.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/16X2fCahLiw?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |

🔥 IS THE GOVERNOR’S RACE SUDDENLY REAL?
The new Journal poll has Haaland at 49% and Hull at 43%, with 8% of voters still undecided.That alone is interesting.But dig into the numbers and it gets even more interesting:• 19% of independents remain undecided
• Hull leads among men by 6 points
• Haaland leads among women by 17
• Hull has a 10-point advantage among voters with a high school/trade-school education
• Haaland has raised roughly $14 million while Hull has been hovering around the $1 million mark
That last number is remarkable.
How does a candidate with that kind of financial advantage find herself only six points ahead?
We break down where Hull still needs to grow, where Haaland remains strong, and the BIG question now: Does this poll convince national Republican groups that New Mexico is worth investing in?
Spoiler alert: The next two weeks could tell us a lot.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/nFiR51ieVzQ?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

💰 NEW MEXICO HAS BILLIONS — BUT WE’RE LOSING PEOPLE?
Here’s a combination of numbers that should get every New Mexican’s attention.New Mexico is projected to bring in $14.8 BILLION in general fund revenue in FY2028, including roughly $924 million in “new money” available to lawmakers.Personal and corporate income-tax projections alone were revised upward by $380 million for FY2027.
Yet another projection shows New Mexico becoming one of only TWO states west of the Mississippi expected to lose population through 2040.
Meanwhile:Texas: +20%
Utah: +21%
Arizona: +14%
Colorado: +12%
New Mexico: roughly -2%
How does a state with our resources, weather, culture and extraordinary natural beauty end up on the shrinking side of that map?
We break down what we believe New Mexico is missing — and why economic growth has to become a much bigger priority for our leaders.

🚨 ICE ARRESTS ARE SURGING
Trump campaigned on dramatically increasing immigration enforcement.Now we’re seeing the numbers. ICE arrests topped 43,000 in June and approached 50,000 in July — more than 1,500 arrests per day and getting closer to the administration’s stated goal of 2,000 per day.
Scott Jennings made a simple point on CNN: For millions of Trump voters, this is exactly what they voted for.
We discuss whether immigration will still move persuadable voters in the midterms — or whether most Americans have already picked a side on this issue.

🇻🇪 DID TRUMP JUST PULL OFF A HUGE VENEZUELA DEAL?This story has been overshadowed by everything happening in Iran, but it could have enormous long-term consequences.
The Trump administration has been negotiating a plan that could give the United States a direct financial stake tied to some of Venezuela’s massive proven oil reserves.
There’s a part of this Mark DOESN’T like: government ownership or stakes in private businesses. But strategically? Reducing China’s influence while increasing American access to one of the world’s largest oil reserves could be a very big deal.
We break down both sides.
🌶️ AND THEN THERE’S... GREEN CHILE.Only in New Mexico.
Police say an argument that began over green chile enchiladas escalated into a fight and ultimately a tragic death in Albuquerque.
We read the details and immediately came to the same conclusion:There HAS to be more to this story.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/Go5d2VfpbT6?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🤢 ELLA FACT-CHECKS GEN ZIs “pheromone maxing” actually a thing?
Reports claim young men are skipping deodorant and showers — and doing things we won’t even repeat here 😳 — because they believe their “natural musk” will make them more attractive. So naturally, we brought in our resident Gen Z representative.
Ella’s verdict?She’s calling fake news on this one. 😂
❤️ AND FINALLY, DOLLY.This one was personal for Krysty. Her mom introduced her to Dolly Parton through songs like “Coat of Many Colors,” and Dolly remained one of those special connections between them.
We share a beautiful clip of Dolly talking about growing up in church, loving Jesus, praying before making decisions and asking God to guide her life.Her words about her mission really say it all: glorify God and uplift people.It’s a sweet way to remember a remarkable woman and the faith that grounded her.
And because it’s Sunday, we finish with Game Day — except this time one of our wildlife cameras caught a BLACK BEAR running across our driveway... in Albuquerque!
Never a dull moment around here.

# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138285166/643648956/1389201924?refcode=AU_NWB_FR_GEN_EOM_AC_20260831_PM1_V1_S1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDY5NjYiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMWJjODg3Y2EtOTFhNS1mMTExLTliMzMtMDAyMjQ4MmE5YThkIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=2Qwt7boX2MbT8yquouRlXno_EuRQGJbOd-mQAWnrPeo=&emci=af709172-8ba5-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&emdi=1bc887ca-91a5-f111-9b33-0022482a9a8d&ceid=35688492)

We got a lot done this month, Peter. In August, my office returned money to homeowners who were charged illegal mortgage fees. We challenged utility costs that could have landed on ratepayers. Peter, I went back and forth on if I should send you this or not. Not because I didn't know what to say, but because I knew how much it would hurt to say it. It’s difficult to admit that I can't do this alone. [**There's so much weighing on me right now, and finding the right words feels impossible. But I'm trusting these words will reach you the way they need to.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/VCDqGcDHoq8PU9e-9Jg9026-37pBdMDm69wHL5OxTj-adDgjLVjW4OCsPXyl2GEn7ohvvAc4Gra5_cywNxUW6rK_G-fzumVbzri0BeVyRNcM2bta1a3zT2Fm5lsM_HxayAnuUDVOa5Pc6m1QirIaflDEBNfL9ysAnylkyDlrd01oXOQRR_ouzyE_8UnNADfk-WxKmscVcNRwoJ17dpdai3xzG-WqI5bd721Fg7KPqo74LxLnO68ACWMjef-YCv04OkJ5qYab3ydjgyTud5cgtYxAUP7qbjM8oxGZ32-sx6ZabqJxFJMdaxa_DyamgwjIUMwTsO2Cs_8jQjdgaeS7P9aK-HmQMDZoGNN8BurjLem0M_4YLkznPeDRM8YBPUWIhBAEigtRjV2L0HOgUCJ3VlRESCpiUVhlGLaE4gHU5rBiLmZGe2UMDUTJAOFyXcfXYPC5S1IumMN5jR_M9HDqINK32n6xEYTKkbHlVdse-q6cXWjED1_YeOjCaSJTHkcNe6RYh6IlZN-Zapz_iDxR8s-PB98_DsIXXV-iDVHT4AQUHDUqSvKdKrA18k8OIqvjJBybuzLy0MTr6T3DYlO0WSPgihDlaGKsJcxxVr-Q7BqMcyqRnHMGvWUkpxqv2ldHjDw-St_G7PVEy9gQPq-tPuZsXfYvvL2SG2frypXvGoODx1ylC9JHndu71fF6pQvnmnHI99RMI1mPIGLNQvfxzzmzk_2qt-XaZYqy__V8Gy6IwftEvUo0DokKbgeYOV8JIsb3eIOyK5oebTNFjzhb4yWCfuoWr3TgaVBYwsxFCjRcQn6GJ2t4CtlOKq6WbXMaRwsMcbU/OpIisa8MkgkSjW4NFiuqWWdWq-rp6ZK8/24) It’s Congressman Brandon Gill. Working cows and driving tractors growing up made me who I am today. It taught me the value of hard work, the importance of keeping your word, and what it means to sacrifice for something bigger than yourself. Trust me, I know all the constant emails and texts can weigh on you. It wears on me too. Some days I wonder if it's worth it. But then I remember why I'm here. I didn't come to Washington because I love asking true patriots like you for money. I didn't run for Congress at 29 years old to become the youngest House Republican so I could spend my nights begging for donations. I came because my kids deserve to grow up in a better America than I grew up in — and right now, that's not guaranteed. Being a husband and a father are the two most important things in my life. Sometimes, when I'm holding my kids, I feel like I'm holding the whole world in my arms. They're everything to me. They're the wind in my sails when it comes to the mission I've committed my life and career to. And at the end of my life, I want to sit before the Father Almighty and declare that I did all I could to leave this great country better off than it was when I grew up. I refuse to look my kids in the eye someday and tell them I gave up when it mattered most. [**That's why I'm still here. That's why I keep sending these messages.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/kqYk4WHdkT18_wu6PAq0dRqJmpVlUPfTC1_Gin6zwQ4YNZilg5m6Msfbuxgvc2oTYOrO7Ja7W7aOdY5D86VgLtZXFACjyKxMc7qFEcQR93toK7xTBhIfZvf6nuGfcKvdxw6428Z1MoUmyuBildEK8s0mnYU9tQtcrf1sggtr2gQApXqxkcfAQuqYnOE16aZoE6ZbSM2IDqWS_ny7qUEe7g1s6MXJzKt7KWS1Bo5pKIjzjUnAOBlJ0jIRzLGgkPFcNjwEnHL9X_1mMOKb9w0dOGWaNaC3EjDndt7uO3rghUhrfiNECpCSX-z0QxXC6UrPJ0DfN8qxAkgMdqPp7Rjm3atdTRsCkVLDwhRptd1s68hzhQylNTMOyJFkKzm5FIA2AiItV-rq5y0F-b0R2WPE75anoiSlofsVr8tHUrFCWY0wYNkACDmFBdr-NRyRBrhLPGMyhxm9ZcWpeTASHNn5pfY9PlsNcMB5pC_kLIxShPRHStA0btPX4Cf7FhmNej_yIIzmgEDHzinXaDbmCoeGwnTEZI33sQWYvVxzCZzuS9t8783t2KfDQKKxXzQNGNZOLXHreGjhRB_USJc5WzgXl2nKG2A9XQeJmfG6puPSS76N_b27AIOUyr9Awaf8cOK0LmjjzQ6muwRpHi5iY5NfqSi2VQIaxrqu7JAcWP6Vju25wHs0uYq9bya0tYQO1ZzSrpLBWyqfcaIlBd2tHqDImbBUlfuVMyZncXtC16e2szbEOn-vwXDgxfx3Jgu0eWEL3APjs3lJQafigYJvVVjj1bSDB1kLAQgJ66pUFEgZoPFFiqpCMlMxsx923CDuON3QMz85h1U/QPFqJixYwA8EscPRyHAuV1x-_gUeF_XQ/24) Because nothing — I repeat — nothing is more important to me than fighting off the vicious leftist attacks against the soul of our country. The left hates you. They hate your vote. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. [**Please, will you take just 1 minute out of your busy schedule to help me continue my fight?**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/7EPhkTA6UtTjBedMvNAkhUxaiKcWqOYjvWqeFbccVXBHylaeO6gL_oz7eJLivFiWo37d-c5BPswa_7tnW7mlV_g2PTcFXTbobEV0chhaaIqLSYrEIc6TZhmaumP7vpgI0la7YNNoASgsDOJ7is41vqUO6M7rjRSGBpn-GaoXWKM5p_Bl9g59M56k6v2_YB_t027jTHgUXbG-Npx6Is9mka5kLnI3Ez0y6Ydbhdm24jtjNgvjxf8s2tAh46_VIqzPzHo_8oWtznyw-MknmCRRHDo389XYB7H0WX9cV7nlF6DeM51VLVDwN1Rx9nv6CDPyJa5SZu6eNKyfqEFpw_dMdZaWFAS51BdyxLsVjJx__RtaTCqC06b2Gb69H5bAQ_wkySzrJnhtl8jNvTkRTLUlym6vh5qadLdwoEXvKSs857MkvDjkZf7wQF9_fjG1i7xO5UDONeQJDVSqfch0GovNRMYE0BOtXWsFCwDCiNuL0tVK7RKnqn63_xRE-xawZSB1Ke5nBoSodeCovTNr1HmZQPfn4PorDU6RgEAVuup4SFl937ivAlgwwpoMRaCkYyO48b_eYTHQPt3F3-g-YsO_aViejAwqrLzVRHJubRyayTDNsV4k_p9Qi6i4DTuDhL7EtzCyOEJGqSJkBb1pj7sUf9Dpwruv5fXQFA01qK8pg3BIE3-mtZCkwV5POfER15KQcAZbkGttwyylrZWT3hdZVzwEQT8EutYKfGeAnH0CeOcu-LRr2cf3Iuvm1VifJ0_zs1PcJUjm7_U-uTGmCQFax2N2GgsHrXsuuSGH0BlnWem3bU1DJXqEDw2YYI3XmbluFDm8cqo/HxcKeStUiYDj-4dR24Mymdu-CEy6KER6/24) This is more than a polite request. They hate MAGA for putting America First. And they will do anything — lie, cheat, steal, destroy — to ensure your children inherit a country you won't even recognize. Peter, today I'll make the same promise to you that I've made to myself, to my wife, and to my children: As long as I live, I will continue to FIGHT to preserve the soul of our country. No force on Earth will push me to abandon my mission and calling. Not the attacks. Not the exhaustion. Not the constant pressure to give up and go home. Believe me, I'm not someone who finds it easy to ask for support. Texting and emailing you like this is the last thing I thought I'd have to do when I ran for Congress. But the country we love is on the brink of destruction, and God has put it on my heart to fight with all that I have — even when that means swallowing my pride and asking for help. This is more than a polite request. This is now a final plea for your support. Sincerely, Congressman Brandon Gill (R) TX-26 | | | Paid for by Brandon Gill for Texas | | PO BOX 827 Arlington, VA 22216 |

More people believe this state doesn't have to stay on this path. But the month is ending and we need you with us to keep building. Please make a contribution today.

Peter - I wanted to reach out quickly to ask if you’d be willing to make a contribution today to help us meet our August fundraising goal. We have to raise another $18,600 by midnight and it’s the last day of my final California legislative session so it’s going to be a late one - but I have to reach out and ask. Can you help by donating now? I’m running for Congress because I’ve spent over a decade proving that you can be a bold, unrelenting Democrat - and still get things done.

I’ve fought to build more affordable housing, take meaningful action on climate change, demand protection for trans youth, embrace innovation while advancing responsible AI standards, and stand up to bigots and bullies - from Elon Musk to Donald Trump.

In this session alone, I’ve sent landmark legislation to the Governor’s desk that will empower Californians to hold ICE accountable for violating their constitutional rights, make it possible for renters to benefit from solar power, and *fingers crossed* advance a multibillion-dollar bond to fund science and research.

We have less than 12 hours now to raise $18K we need for the next week of our campaign.

Please, help me keep fighting for these values by donating to support my Congressional campaign at this critical moment - we really can’t miss this moment.

Whatever you can do - it helps.

Texas hasn't elected a Democrat to the United States Senate since 1988. Thirty-eight years. And today, Fox News looked at the data and said: this race is a coin flip. That should alarm every conservative in this country. It certainly alarms me. But there's more. Fox News also moved the Michigan Senate race, where DSA-backed Abdul El-Sayed just won his primary, from "Lean Democrat" to "toss-up." **_Two races. Two toss-ups. Announced on the same day_.** Now let me show you the number that explains everything. In Texas, James Talarico has $27.5 million in the bank. **_Ken Paxton, our Republican nominee, has $6.9 million_.** That is not a gap. That is a canyon. Talarico has $3 to every $1 the cash of the Republican candidate in the state of Texas. 3:1. And it shows -- it shows in the polling, it shows in the ads running on Texas television, and it shows in a Fox News forecast that just moved one of the reddest states in America to a coin flip. _This is what happens when one side is sufficiently funded and the other is not._ Democrats need four seats to take back the Senate majority. They have two toss-ups,Texas and Michigan, right in front of them. They are not going to stop. They are not going to slow down. And Chuck Schumer has spent years and hundreds of millions of dollars building the machine that is executing this plan right now. I have been fighting this fight on two fronts.
